records.abstract: Multimodal brain tumor segmentation from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) underpins radiotherapy target delineation, surgical planning, and treatment follow-up, but remains limited by costly voxel-wise annotation with imperfect inter-rater agreement, domain shift driven by cross-center differences in scanners and acquisition protocols, and marked subregional heterogeneity with unstable performance on small enhancing components. To support generalizable, explainable, and clinically deployable systems, this paper reviews the past decade of brain tumor MRI segmentation and offers a unified, critical comparison using a five-dimensional framework: target of interest, optimization objective, core mechanism, key assumptions, and typical failure modes. We summarize the supervised-learning mainstream based on encoder–decoder architectures and key advances enabled by attention constraints and multimodal fusion. We further analyze three emerging paradigms: self-supervised learning leverages unlabeled data but is challenged by medical semantic alignment and the cost of three-dimensional pretraining; privacy-preserving multi-center collaborative learning improves compliance but must balance heterogeneous data, communication overhead, and privacy-induced performance loss; and graph-based relational modeling encodes structural priors yet is hindered by graph-construction errors, scalability, and limited verifiable explanations. Finally, we identify gaps in data and evaluation standardization, cross-center generalization, robustness for small subregions, trustworthy evidence chains, and deployment constraints, and we propose an actionable roadmap and a minimum clinical closed-loop recommendation to align future work across accuracy, robustness, privacy, and clinical usability.

records.abstract: Physics-informed neural operators are a promising framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) by integrating physical laws into neural network architectures. However, existing methods such as physics-informed DeepONet (PI-DeepONet) struggle to generalize under complex geometric variations because they encode spatial coordinates independently of the geometry. In this study, we propose a geometry-adaptive physics-informed DeepONet (GAPI-DeepONet) that effectively captures geometry-dependent nonlinearities by integrating a generalized geometry representation into the branch network and modulating the trunk network through a geometry-adaptive conditioning network. Unlike naïve PI-DeepONet or existing embedding approaches, the proposed method is designed to more efficiently capture geometry-dependent nonlinear behaviors by directly modulating the geometry-sensitive features of the trunk network through trainable geometry-adaptive parameters. By applying layer-wise modulation to the trunk features, this architecture can effectively handle a wider range of geometric configurations while maintaining training efficiency. We evaluate the performance of the proposed model on three representative problems, including flow around a cylinder, NACA (National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics) airfoil flow, and a three-dimensional heat sink, with conventional PI-DeepONet, Fourier Neural Operator (FNO), and ResUNet-based DeepONet. The proposed GAPI-DeepONet consistently outperforms comparative models both for accuracy and robustness, achieving up to a 90% reduction in the L2 relative error and demonstrating its capability to resolve fine-scale variations under varying geometric conditions. These results highlight its potential for real-time simulation and further optimization tasks in many engineering problems involving complex geometric variations.

records.abstract: Multimodal neuroimaging data provide complementary structural and functional information for Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis. However, acquiring a large-scale multimodal dataset with precise annotations is resource-intensive and incurs substantial costs. Effectively fusing relevant information across modalities also remains a significant challenge. Existing methods are often constrained by modeling intra-modality specific features and inter-modal shared information in isolation, overlooking their critical interactions. Additionally, the heterogeneity among modalities introduces a major obstacle to achieving reliable cross-modality feature alignment. To tackle these problems, we propose an end-to-end semi-supervised multimodal fusion framework with adversarial contrastive learning. Specifically, a pseudo-labeling strategy is designed to make full use of unlabeled data by regulating the quality of pseudo-labels with a threshold. To adaptively capture inter-modal shared characteristics while preserving the unique properties of intra-modality, we design a Dual-phase Inter–Intra Attention Fusion Unit that effectively exploits the interactions between different modalities. Moreover, to achieve efficient alignment of multimodal data at both the feature and subject levels, we develop a hierarchical alignment strategy based on adversarial contrastive learning. This strategy maps features into a shared latent space and promotes the proximity of inter-modal paired samples within that space, thereby simultaneously mitigating distributional discrepancies and resolving semantic inconsistencies across modalities. Extensive experiments conducted on two independent public datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework performs excellently in AD diagnosis compared with existing approaches, notably achieving an accuracy of 92.00 (±1.00)% on ADNI1 with only 40% labels.

records.abstract: Biofilters are widely used to remove volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from industrial exhaust streams, yet their real-world performance often deteriorates before the end of the planned service period due to media aging, moisture imbalance, and increasing pressure drop. Most existing design and optimization approaches treat the filter bed as static and focus on short-term removal efficiency, while ignoring (i) time-dependent degradation, (ii) the practical trade-off between efficiency, longevity, and operational burden, and (iii) uncertainty and limited experimental data that make optimization recommendations fragile when operating conditions change. As a result, solutions that look optimal in a snapshot can lead to rapid decline and frequent maintenance in long-term operation. This paper proposes an adaptive, multi-objective optimization framework for long-term biofilter media design and operation. The method learns how removal performance evolves over time and uses this predictive capability to search for implementable media ”recipes” and operating setpoints that jointly maximize removal efficiency and stability while limiting pressure drop and experimental cost. The framework is validated on three physically built modular biofilters (135 observations per configuration; 405 total) treating acetone as a representative oxygenated VOC, including a three-stage design with a zeolite buffering layer. The best optimized configuration achieved high initial and sustained performance (initial removal up to 94.7% and median removal up to 88.89%) with an extended operational lifetime of up to 301 days, while exhibiting slower performance deterioration with less negative degradation slopes (from -0.0160% day-1 to -0.00916% day-1) compared to conventional media selection and standard optimizers.

records.abstract: The variation of roll angle in a multi-axle intelligent wheeled vehicle is a critical factor for the vehicle safety control system. However, classical dynamic models exhibit significant errors under non-steady-state conditions and are computationally complex due to their high degrees of freedom. Meanwhile, data-driven deep learning networks often struggle with poor recognition performance under data loss or zero-sample conditions. To improve roll angle recognition accuracy across various operating conditions, this study proposes an attention improved physics-informed long short-term memory (Attention-PI-LSTM). The proposed deep learning neural network also shows better performance of value prediction with sensor-noise or data loss, even with zero-sampling portion training data, the predict function of the Attention-PI-LSTM still maintains an acceptable accuracy level. The algorithm is validated through simulation using real-world data collected from a 4-axle intelligent wheeled vehicle. Firstly, a vehicle roll angle dynamics model considering axle load transfer during steering was established. Secondly, the physics-informed long short-term memory (PI-LSTM) network is developed with a physics-informed loss function derived from the dynamics model. Finally, adopted attention mechanism to the PI-LSTM algorithm to assign weights to sequential input data. Experiment results show that the proposed Attention-PI-LSTM algorithm improves the coefficient of determination (R^{2}) by 27.4% compared to the regular deep learning neural networks. It also maintains recognition accuracy of 0.651 and 0.694 under data loss and zero-sample conditions, respectively.

records.abstract: This study presents a heuristic physics-informed neural network (H-PINN) architecture based on artificial intelligence (AI) to simulate the melting-driven thin-film flow of a Cross fluid over an inclined sheet, which is affected by industrial waste and electroosmotic impacts. The flow behavior is affected by the combined impacts of joule heating, quadratic thermal radiation, heat generation, viscous dissipation, Darcy-Forchheimer, velocity slip conditions, and temperature-dependent thermal conductivity. Reduce the governing nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) to a set of linked ordinary differential equations (ODEs) using the proper similarity transformations. The physics-informed neural network (PINN) method uses global optimizers like particle swarm optimization (PSO) and the neural network algorithm (NNA) to change the network's weights and biases, which helps find solutions faster and more accurately. The results show that increasing the electroosmotic and unsteady parameters enhances the velocity profile by approximately 34% and 27.27%, respectively, while heat generation, impurity-induced thermal changes, and Eckert number effects have a substantial impact on the temperature distribution by about 32%, 18%, and 45%, respectively. The concentration profile declined by around 15% as the unsteady parameter rose, whereas waste discharge enhanced it by nearly 40%. The melting heat parameter enhances the heat transfer rate, while the pollutant parameter declines the mass transfer rate. The mean squared errors (MSE) and Theil Inequality Coefficient (TIC) decrease from 10^{−6} to 10^{−9}, indicating that they are accurate, and well optimized. The meshless technique is a viable alternative to the fourth-order collocation method for boundary value problems (BVP4c). This AI-driven modeling framework can simulate and optimize complex transport phenomena in industrial thin-film coating, aerospace applications, and microscale bio-fluidic systems.

records.abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) play a critical role in renewable energy, transportation, and industrial drives due to their high efficiency and reliability. Whereas thermal-induced demagnetization under high-temperature conditions can lead to irreversible performance loss, maintenance in current systems is predominantly reactive. To address this limitation, this study proposes a physics-informed framework that integrates an extended Arrhenius degradation model with a feedforward neural network (FNN). The framework explicitly captures the nonlinear coupling between temperature and exposure time, enabling prediction of the demagnetization trend at given thermal condition. Uncertainty quantification is achieved via Monte Carlo parameter perturbations, from which 95% confidence intervals (CI) are constructed to improve prediction reliability. A probabilistic safety-boundary method then classifies material health states and determines the maximum safe operating time. Experimental validation demonstrates that the proposed approach reduces prediction error, enabling more effective maintenance planning. The framework thus offers a robust tool for assessing and mitigating demagnetization risks in high-temperature environments.

records.abstract: Mechanical metastructures offer promising applications in energy-absorbing devices and soft actuators. However, their highly nonlinear responses, especially sudden force drop within a quite narrow displacement range, pose a significant challenge in accurate prediction and inverse optimization. This study introduces a feature-driven machine learning approach that significantly enhances the predictive accuracy and efficiency of highly nonlinear responses. Herein, bistable twist metastructures with highly nonlinear sudden force drop responses are utilized as the platform. By employing feature-driven classification and reconstruction, force-displacement curves are modularized according to the feature types. The feature-driven sampling strategy increases the sampling density in highly nonlinear modules while reducing the redundant points in approximately linear modules. This facilitates the optimized distribution of sampling points in each module, ensuring the integrity of highly nonlinear features. Moreover, the feature-driven machine learning approach reduces the severe reliance on large data amount. Utilizing only 1500 data groups, a mapping paradigm between 9 geometric parameters and highly nonlinear responses is established through machine learning within only 1∼3 min, achieving a significantly higher accuracy. Additionally, inverse design is accomplished through the integration of trained network and search algorithms. Targeted on the pronounced structural hysteresis, which is advantageous to cushioning performance, desired mechanical responses are identified, exhibiting an enhancement exceeding 30%, with the corresponding geometric parameters effectively determined. It is believed that this feature-driven modular approach holds immense potentials for both precise prediction and effective optimization of mechanical metastructures with highly nonlinear responses.

records.abstract: Model-based offline reinforcement learning (RL) offers a safe and efficient approach for trajectory tracking of underactuated autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). This approach addresses the problems of high risk and low efficiency in training within real environments. However, model construction requires a large amount of real data, the reality gap may lead to control failure, and resisting external disturbances is also challenging. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a data-efficient control framework based on physics-informed offline RL to enable underactuated AUVs to track trajectories in variable ocean current environments. First, a data-efficient modeling method utilizing ensemble physics-informed neural networks is introduced to develop an AUV physics-informed model from limited real data. This model is utilized to train the RL-based controller, enabling long-term, high-precision state prediction and uncertainty quantification within the real data distribution. Then, we propose a prioritized replay-based offline conservative policy optimization method. This approach utilizes prioritized replay combined with a constrained training process to generate reliable synthetic data. By learning a conservative policy to overcome the reality gap, the RL-based controller achieves zero-shot sim-to-real transfer. Furthermore, a two-stage control scheme is designed to resist variable ocean current disturbances without requiring additional compensation by formulating each controller as a Markov decision process with a well-designed state, action, and reward. Finally, the results of simulation and field tests demonstrate that the proposed control framework achieves trajectory tracking performance comparable to that of traditional methods under ocean current disturbances, relying on only 400 data samples.

records.abstract: Underwater object detection is essential for marine research, ecological monitoring, and autonomous underwater operations, where accurate object identification supports ecosystem analysis, resource management, and exploration. However, underwater environments pose significant challenges, including poor visibility, cluttered backgrounds, class imbalance, and difficulty in extracting discriminative features. To address these issues using advanced Artificial Intelligence techniques for marine environmental monitoring, the Dynamic Generative Adversarial Network Augmented Cross-Shaped Window Transformer framework is introduced as a robust and adaptive solution for underwater object detection. The proposed framework incorporates deep learning–based Artificial Intelligence methods, including Generative Adversarial Network–based data augmentation, to generate diverse and high-quality synthetic underwater images. This strategy mitigates data scarcity and class imbalance while improving robustness against turbidity, uneven illumination, and occlusion. A Dynamic Graph Attention Span mechanism is embedded within the Cross-Shaped Window Transformer to enable adaptive attention windows and enhance modeling of complex object relationships. The Adaptive Feature Refinement Module improves detection performance by emphasizing underrepresented and small-scale object classes. The Attention and Super-Resolution Assisted Module selectively enhance feature resolution in critical regions, while the Adaptive Detection and Feedback Module introduce an iterative feedback loop that refines detection accuracy dynamically. Extensive experiments conducted on the DeepFish and DUO datasets demonstrate strong effectiveness in Artificial Intelligence driven underwater object detection for marine ecosystem monitoring. The framework achieves high performance across mean Average Precision, Matthews Correlation Coefficient, Dice Similarity Coefficient, Jaccard Index, and Structural Similarity Index Measure metrics, outperforming existing state-of-the-art underwater object detection methods.

records.abstract: Brain tumors are life-threatening, making early and accurate diagnosis crucial. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is widely used for its high-quality, radiation-free imaging. However, the increasing volume of images and the variability in tumor size, shape and location make manual analysis both time-consuming and impractical. These challenges have driven the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and deep learning to improve diagnostic precision. By integrating advanced training algorithms and data augmentation techniques, these technologies aim to achieve more accurate and efficient brain tumor analysis. This paper proposes two-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (2D CNN) models based on backpropagation and the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) training algorithms, along with data augmentation using rotation, shifting, flipping, and brightness adjustments before resizing the samples for the model, and compares their performance with the Adam optimizer backpropagation algorithm. The proposed lightweight EKF-based 2D CNN Keras model shows strong performance with 40 times lower complexity than existing models. The EKF-based model reached 95.63% accuracy during testing. The model was also retrained on an additional database, achieving 93.16% test accuracy, and subsequently validated on a separate, third database, reaching 91.89% accuracy, confirming robustness and generalization. The model converges quickly, and has been implemented on a Virtual Private Server (VPS) with Python Fast Application Programming Interface framework (FastAPI) and an Android application for seamless data acquisition and instant inference. These features make it a strong candidate for clinical use, particularly in resource-limited settings such mobile health units.

records.abstract: Time series anomaly detection plays an important role in various fields, such as abnormal driving behaviors in autonomous driving, predictive maintenance in manufacturing, and network security for Cyber–Physical Systems, etc. Most anomaly detectors are reconstruction-based methods utilizing Autoencoders to reconstruct time series. However, these methods are relatively difficult to obtain a high-quality reconstructed sequence applicable for anomaly detection between poor and excessive reconstruction. To address this issue, we propose a novel Reconstruction-based Anomaly Detection method with Diffusion Models (ReADD). More concretely, it employs the inherent characteristics of diffusion models by adding noise to the original data and then crafts a denoising network considering feature information instead of the comprehensive assessment of feature and temporal dependencies to obtain the reconstructed sequence. ReADD redefines the reconstruction process through diffusion models, whose goal is not to directly optimize the similarity between input and output, but to enhance the distinction between normal points and anomalies by disrupting the anomalies. Numerous experiments on four real-world datasets, Mars Science Laboratory rover (MSL), Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP), Pooled Server Metrics (PSM), and Secure Water Treatment (SWaT) demonstrate that our proposed ReADD obtains superior performance compared to other reconstruction-based anomaly detection approaches. In particular, ReADD achieves an average improvement of 7.01% in Precision (P), 6.23% in Recall (R), and 6.87% in F1-Score (F1), respectively.

records.abstract: Single-molecule three-dimensional (3D) real-time tracking is crucial for addressing key scientific questions, including viral infection mechanisms, interactions between nanodrugs and target cells, and the laws governing interactions among nucleic acid macromolecules. However, reconstructing 3D multi-molecule motion trajectories remains a major challenge in this technology, which restricts its applications in molecular biology and cell biology. A novel artificial intelligence-based image processing technique has been developed to address the prevalent issues of suboptimal detection accuracy, tracking drift, and the labour-intensive processes associated with conventional nanoparticle tracking methodologies. First, a generative adversarial network (GAN) is employed to enhance low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) images by suppressing background noise while preserving fine structural details. Then, You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8), a real-time object detection algorithm, is applied to accurately locate nanoparticles in each frame. Finally, Better Tracking by Association (ByteTrack) associates detected particles across consecutive frames to reconstruct continuous motion trajectories. This deep neural network-based multimolecular 3D motion trajectory reconstruction algorithm features high-fidelity image denoising, accurate target detection, and precise particle tracking and matching. In this study, a 3D particle imaging technique based on double-helix phase modulation is used to observe nanoparticles suspended in a glycerol solution, effectively capturing foundational images of particle dynamics. Subsequently, the proposed GAN–YOLOv8–Track algorithm is employed to reconstruct the 3D trajectories of these nanoparticles. Experimental results show that our model outperforms traditional methods in tracking stability, detection accuracy, and operational simplicity.

records.abstract: This paper proposes an improved deep learning network, Channel-Fusion U-shaped Convolutional Network (CF-UNet), for building extraction tasks. CF-UNet is built upon the classic U-shaped Convolutional Neural Network (U-Net) architecture, incorporating innovative designs to enhance feature extraction accuracy and robustness. In the encoder, the Mobile Inverted Bottleneck Convolution (MBConv) module is introduced to capture multi-scale features while reducing computational complexity. In the skip connections, a Channel-Fusion (CF) module is designed, which integrates channel attention (CA) and spatial attention (SA) to strengthen the extraction of boundary features and key regions. In the decoder, the Attention-augmented Convolution Mix (ACMix) mechanism is embedded, leveraging the advantages of self-attention and convolution operations to improve global context modeling and local detail representation. Extensive experiments on both the Wuhan University Building Extraction (WHUBuilding) dataset and the Massachusetts Buildings dataset demonstrate that CF-UNet outperforms existing methods in key metrics, including Precision (Pre), Recall (Re), mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), and Overall Accuracy (OA). Notably, CF-UNet exhibits superior performance in complex background conditions and multi-scale building scenarios. The proposed model provides a novel technical solution for building extraction and holds significant practical application value in the field of Artificial Intelligence for remote sensing and geospatial analysis.

records.abstract: Accurate estimation of state of health (SOH) is critical for ensuring the operational safety and long-term reliability of large-scale lithium-ion battery energy storage systems (BESS). However, existing approaches remain limited by insufficient real-world operational data and a general lack of physical interpretability. To overcome these constraints, this study analyzes an industrial dataset comprising 8.3 million data points collected over 240 days from a 1000 kW-hour BESS with 1296 cells, which reveals significant cluster-level SOH inconsistencies linked to electrical topology. Building on this analysis, we propose a convolutional physics-informed neural network (CPNN), which integrates battery degradation physics with deep convolutional learning. This artificial intelligence (AI)-based model eliminates the need for manual feature engineering while ensuring physical consistency. Experimental results demonstrate that the CPNN reduces the average mean absolute percentage error by 32.67% across four distinct datasets compared to conventional convolutional neural networks. Furthermore, our data-driven analysis identifies electrical design factors underpinning heterogeneous aging patterns, offering actionable insights for the design optimization of BESS. This work not only advances AI-driven methodologies for battery prognostics but also addresses pivotal engineering challenges in BESS lifecycle management.

records.abstract: Radiology report generation remains challenging in artificial intelligence due to the semantic gap between medical images and diagnostic narratives and the lack of clinical interpretability in current models. To address these issues, we propose a novel cognitive-driven multimodal framework that integrates hierarchical visual-semantic alignment with radiologist-inspired attention mechanism. Specifically, we extract pixel, region, and organ level features using Vision Transformer (ViT) and align them with Radiology Lexicon (RadLex)-based medical concepts to enhance anatomical grounding. Our model incorporates knowledge-enhanced multi-label classification module to jointly predict diagnostic labels during report generation. This component is designed using novel Multi-path Interaction Expansion Multilayer Perceptron (MIX-MLP) structure, which improves robustness to noisy or incomplete labels by enabling residual feature refinement across classification stages. Beyond serving as an auxiliary loss, this module provides interpretable intermediate supervision. These predicted labels are embedded and fused with visual and textual features through Radiological Cognitive Triangular Attention (RCTA) module, which simulates the iterative reasoning process of radiologists. Experimental results on two benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of our method. On Indiana University Chest X-ray Collection (IU-Xray), our model achieves Consensus-based Image Description Evaluation (CIDEr) score of 0.654 (25.0%), while on Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care Chest X-Ray (MIMIC-CXR), it reaches a CIDEr score of 0.397 (47.5%), outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. Furthermore, the generated reports exhibit improved semantic accuracy, clinical consistency, and label-text alignment. These results demonstrate that our method effectively bridges the semantic gap in medical report generation and holds promise for real-world clinical applications. Our code is available at https://github.com/jiasyang/Hi-CliTR.

records.abstract: The mechanical behavior of geotechnical materials is mathematically characterized through constitutive models, which are typically formulated based on a priori assumptions and theoretical deductions to effectively address a wide range of engineering challenges. Given the inherent complexity of soil, a trade-off exists between the accuracy of these models and their practical applicability in engineering applications. This study introduces a modeling framework that incorporates physical constraints into symbolic regression (SR). By utilizing finite mathematical operators and variables, the framework guides the optimization process from both physical and mechanical perspectives, yielding a concise yet robust description of constitutive models. Comparative evaluations against purely data-driven models and classical physics-based models indicate that the integration of physical and mechanical constraints significantly improves the efficiency and effectiveness of model optimization. The proposed approach achieves high predictive accuracy while maintaining low model complexity, without requiring high-resolution input data. This hybrid modeling framework effectively balances physical discovery with data fitting, demonstrating robust generalization and extrapolation capabilities.

records.abstract: Accurate real-time modeling of lithium-ion battery electrochemical dynamics is critical for battery management systems (BMS), yet traditional approaches struggle to balance mechanistic fidelity with computational efficiency. To address this, we propose an artificial intelligence (AI) method based on a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) framework formulated upon the Single Particle Model (SPM). Methodologically, the study introduces three core innovations: (1) a Multi-scale Adaptive Fourier Encoding (MSAFE) architecture that eliminates gradient conflicts across stiff spatiotemporal dynamics; (2) a functional Hard Constraint formulation explicitly guaranteeing exact Neumann boundary satisfaction without residual accumulation; and (3) a decoupled two-stage causal training strategy. As a specific engineering application of this method, the framework reconstructs complete spatiotemporal radial concentration fields and predicts terminal voltage. Validation is performed against high-fidelity Doyle-Fuller-Newman (DFN) simulations using the authoritative Python Battery Mathematical Modelling (PyBaMM) framework with a widely-adopted benchmark commercial parameter set. Despite the reduced-order physics basis, the model demonstrates precise internal state estimation, achieving relative errors of 2.31% for internal radial distribution and 1.56% for surface distribution during dynamic discharge transients. Furthermore, the model exhibits robust generalization to unseen operating conditions, achieving a discharge voltage Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 6.10 mV (mV) that surpasses training accuracy by 20.6%. This performance confirms that physics constraints effectively smooth the learning manifold against overfitting, maintaining 97.1% thermodynamic consistency with millisecond-level inference speeds, establishing a foundational methodology for reliable real-time deployment.

records.abstract: In recent years, Transformer-based models have achieved strong performance in image super-resolution (SR). However, their high computational complexity and parameter cost still limit deployment on resource-constrained devices. To better balance efficiency and representation capability, this paper proposes a lightweight Transformer for image super-resolution, termed Multi-Window Attention Transformer for Image Super-Resolution (MWAT-SR), which adopts a hierarchical multi-window attention strategy. In shallow layers, Local Dense Attention (LDA) with small windows is used to preserve local high-frequency details. In deeper layers, larger windows are introduced together with a Hybrid Sparse-Channel Attention (HSCA) mechanism, which combines sparse spatial interaction and channel-wise semantic modeling to enlarge the effective receptive field under controlled computational cost. In addition, a Window-Adaptive Multi-Scale Convolutional Feed-Forward Network (WAMC-FFN) is designed to adjust convolution kernel sizes according to the window scale, thereby enhancing multi-scale texture representation. Experimental results on standard benchmark datasets show that MWAT-SR achieves competitive reconstruction performance across \times 2$\times 2$, \times 3$\times 3$, and \times 4$\times 4$ settings, while maintaining a favorable trade-off between reconstruction quality and computational complexity.

records.abstract: The accurate prediction of material properties is critical for accelerating materials discovery and design. Machine Learning methods, particularly graph neural networks, have recently demonstrated promising results in modeling the structural and electronic characteristics of crystalline materials. However, performance can degrade in deep architectures and structurally complex materials and capturing subtle structural dependencies remains challenging. In this work, we introduce a Differential Attention Transformer-enhanced Graph Neural Network that integrates chemically informed structural features with a dual-attention mechanism. Our approach follows a structure framework, beginning with collection and preprocessing of crystal structures further incorporates a learning architecture combining self- and differential-attention, residual graph convolutions and chemically-informed positional encodings to model complex atomic interactions. When evaluated on benchmark Materials Project datasets for bandgap and formation energy prediction, proposed method up to an 8% reduction in mean absolute error for formation energy and a 5% reduction for bandgap compared with recent graph neural network-based approaches. These results indicate that proposed method provides an accurate and scalable framework for crystal-structure-informed property prediction, contributing to continued progress in data-driven materials informatics.

records.abstract: To address the small, noisy, and heterogeneous datasets that hinder durability prediction of fiber reinforced polymer bar reinforced seawater and sea-sand concrete beams in marine environments, this study develops a physics guided machine learning framework for predicting durability related structural responses under marine exposure. The framework combines a physics structured operator for mechanistic guidance, a residual learning module for error correction, and an ensemble based meta knowledge branch for improved feature representation. A curated dataset of 89 beam specimens compiled from seven published studies and one experimental campaign conducted by the authors was used for model development and validation. Compared with conventional tree based models, the proposed framework significantly improves regression accuracy, reducing the root mean square error from 6.16 kN to 2.00 kN for ultimate load and from 4.45 mm to 1.75 mm for ultimate deflection, with corresponding coefficients of determination of 0.998 and 0.977. Additional tests under reduced training size and noise injection further demonstrate strong data efficiency and robustness. Overall, the proposed framework provides an accurate and practical approach for durability assessment of fiber reinforced polymer bar reinforced seawater and sea-sand concrete beams in marine environments.

records.abstract: The accuracy of vision-based displacement measurement is critically dependent on image quality, a requirement often difficult to satisfy under outdoor challenges such as illumination variation and optical turbulence. To address this issue, this paper proposes a cost-effective method for enhancing the measurement accuracy based on deep learning-based image Ruper-Resolution (SR). The method comprises three key components: (1)Developing a real-world Low Resolution (LR)-High Resolution (HR) image pair dataset via image acquisition, image registration, template matching and data augmentation; (2)Performing image SR reconstruction using an improved Enhanced Deep Super-Resolution (EDSR) model that integrates Parallel Multi-Scale Convolutional (PMSC) and Channel Attention Block (CAB) modules into the EDSR baseline; (3)Conducting structural displacement identification using the Kanade-Lucas-Tomasi (KLT) algorithm on the reconstructed SR images. The proposed method was validated through an indoor shear test of a bridge bearing and an outdoor vibration test of a suspension bridge model. The results show that, in terms of image quality, the improved EDSR outperforms the original EDSR. It improves the Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) by 3.2% and the Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) by 2.5% in indoor test, and improves PSNR by 2.6% and SSIM by 0.6% in outdoor test. For displacement measurement, compared with the results obtained from LR video, the proposed method significantly enhances accuracy, reducing the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) by 37.4% in indoor test and 27% in outdoor test. These validation results demonstrate that the method can effectively mitigate image degradation in field environments and further improve displacement measurement accuracy.

records.abstract: As a typical application of artificial intelligence (AI), automated medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in numerous scenarios such as clinical diagnosis and auxiliary treatment. However, supervised medical image segmentation relies on abundant labeled data, which is expensive and time-consuming to obtain. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as a promising engineering framework in this context to alleviate the annotation burden by leveraging abundant unlabeled data. However, existing SSL methods suffer from inadequate feature representation and high prediction uncertainty, which will cause blurred boundaries in complex anatomical structures and compromise diagnostic accuracy. To address these issues, we propose a semi-supervised medical image segmentation framework by integrating dual-view graph contrastive learning (DGCL) and latent space uncertainty rectification (LSUR) strategy. The DGCL constructs a topological graph in the feature space by adaptively linking high-entropy anchor points, which explicitly enforces the intra-class compactness and inter-class discriminability to enhance the structural semantic information extraction along decision boundaries. Complementarily, LSUR performs generative reconstruction and refinement in the latent space for high uncertainty regions, which significantly mitigates the error accumulation caused by pseudo-labels, and enhances model robustness and prediction accuracy. Extensive experiments on public datasets demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art comparison methods on different evaluation metrics with 10% and 30% labeled data. This indicates that the proposed method provides an effective AI-driven solution for accurate clinical segmentation with limited annotations.

records.abstract: Predicting concrete failure under high-impact loads is critical for designing protective structures. Machine learning models can provide high predictive accuracy, but they often lack robustness when applied to out-of-distribution data. Traditional physics-based methods cannot fully resolve this limitation because concrete failure under impact loading is highly nonlinear and difficult to describe with complete physical accuracy. To address this challenge, this study proposes a Mixture of Physics-Informed Expert system, an artificial intelligence and deep-learning framework for predicting concrete failure behavior under high-impact loading. The proposed system uses physics-based gating logic and a dynamic regularization strategy to improve prediction reliability when the input conditions differ from the training data. The system was evaluated for penetration depth prediction and achieved a coefficient of determination of 0.9884. It also reduced the mean absolute error by 9.7% compared with a standard neural network and by 68.0% compared with common empirical formulas. These results show that the proposed artificial intelligence approach can balance data-driven accuracy with physics-based reliability for robust prediction of concrete failure behavior in critical engineering applications.

records.abstract: Metamaterials enable advanced applications in compact, high-performance systems, such as soft robotics and mechanical neural networks, where continuous and independent tuning of effective properties is essential. Achieving such control requires solving the inverse-design problem of generating meso-scale geometries that realize prescribed material properties. However, conventional topology optimization often struggles with simultaneous multi-property control and smooth structural transitions, while existing machine-learning-based generative models typically lack interpretable latent representations and reliable epistemic uncertainty quantification. To address these challenges, we propose an interpretable and uncertainty-aware representation-learning framework for metamaterial inverse design. The framework embeds effective elastic material properties directly into structured latent dimensions, enabling continuous and decoupled property tuning with smooth geometric interpolation. An auxiliary surface-mapping mechanism quantifies epistemic uncertainty through predictive performance consistency, providing a reliability indicator for each generated design. The case study demonstrates a strong correlation between the estimated epistemic uncertainty and the actual design error for target elastic effective properties, validating its effectiveness for reliability assessment. The proposed approach further supports efficient exploration of the material property space, continuously decoupled property tuning and uncertainty-aware multi-lattice topology optimization. These results establish a trustworthy and interpretable paradigm for inverse design of metamaterials with controllable properties.

records.abstract: Assembly contact interface characteristics critically influence the performance of precision mechanical systems. Traditional design methods relying on iterative finite element analysis are computationally expensive, while existing deep learning approaches often neglect physical constraints and the complex effects of assembly processes. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a physics-constrained deep learning framework for the inverse design of assembly interfaces. Specifically, we introduce a novel network architecture which integrates multi-source inputs including target contact pressure, assembly parameters, and service conditions. To enforce physical consistency, a differentiable loss function incorporating the impenetrability condition is developed. Furthermore, an optimized learning rate scheduling strategy is implemented to enhance model convergence. Comprehensive ablation and comparative experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms conventional approaches in both accuracy and physical plausibility. When applied to an aero-engine flange structure, the framework enables rapid inverse design of interface morphology, reducing maximum contact pressure by 15.67% and increasing the effective contact area by 45.23% compared to traditional designs. This work provides a robust solution for assembly interface design and advances the application of physics-constrained deep learning in complex engineering systems.

records.abstract: Recently, indoor object detection (OD) and distance estimation in an Internet of Things (IoT) environment have gained significant attention, integrating smart sensors, cameras, and connected devices to accurately detect and localize objects in enclosed spaces. OD is an important and effective technology across various fields because it can automatically detect and recognise objects and images. New developments in useful technology have mainly concentrated on improving navigation and object recognition. Using computer vision, machine learning, and sensor fusion techniques, the system can identify different object classes, estimate distances, and communicate data over the IoT network for surveillance, automation, and safety applications. Now, deep learning techniques are widely used for distance estimation and OD processes. In this paper, a Deep Learning with Convolutional Feature Representation for Indoor Object Detection and Distance Estimation (DLCFR-IODDE) approach is presented in an IoT environment. The paper aims to develop an IoT-based OD and distance estimation for indoor environments. To begin with, the image pre-processing phase employs a Gaussian filter to improve image quality. Furthermore, Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network method is used for the OD process. To achieve effective feature extraction, the DLCFR-IODDE method uses the Swin Transformer to capture both local and global features from image data. Moreover, graph convolutional network model is implemented for classification. Finally, distance estimation process uses the inverse depth regression model. To demonstrate the improved performance of the DLCFR-IODDE method, a comprehensive empirical study is conducted on the Indoor OD dataset. The comparison analysis of the DLCFR-IODDE method showed an accuracy of 99.77% compared with existing methods.

records.abstract: High-precision wavefront interferometry is extremely sensitive to environmental vibrations, which limits the industrial deployment of conventional phase-shifting interferometers. In this paper, an anti-vibration wavefront interferometry (AVWI) framework using only one or two interferograms is proposed. AVWI reduces the reliance on vibration-isolated environments and high-precision phase shifters by explicitly decoupling vibration-induced errors from the test wavefront. This is enabled by a vibration-detection model based on a physics-informed U-Net (AVWI-PIUN). The network learns vibration information from interferograms and enforces cross-frame consistency among phase-shifted interferograms. A physics-informed loss, denoted as {\mathcal{L}}_{Phy}${\mathcal{L}}_{Phy}$, is further introduced using partial-derivative relationships between phase-shifted interferograms, which significantly reduces the required training data and accelerates convergence. Experiments under vibrating conditions demonstrate that AVWI achieves superior accuracy, repeatability, and efficiency compared with a temporal phase-shifting method. Specifically, AVWI achieves a Q peak-to-valley (PVq) figure error of 13.750 nm (nm), a root mean square (RMS) figure error of 1.784 nm, and an RMS repeatability of 0.411 nm, corresponding to reductions of 50.1%, 76.0%, and 92.2%, respectively. In addition, AVWI tolerates phase-shifting errors up to ±9π/20. These results indicate that AVWI provides a practical route toward nanometer-level surface figure metrology in vibration-prone industrial and in-situ machining environments.

records.abstract: Hull blocks, as fundamental assembly units in vessel construction, require specialized transporters due to their substantial size and weight. Optimizing the scheduling of these transporters is crucial for ensuring on-time production and improving operational efficiency in shipyard logistics. Accordingly, this study proposes a scheduling approach that minimizes block transport tardiness and empty travel time. While previous studies have primarily focused on transport scheduling using metaheuristic algorithms, this study introduces a scalable and dynamic scheduling algorithm that employs reinforcement learning integrated with the Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Network (CGCNN). CGCNN is used to encode edge-attributed graphs for state representation, effectively capturing the importance of each location. The proposed algorithm demonstrates stable and superior performance compared to existing priority rules and metaheuristic algorithms across diverse problem distributions, demonstrating its generalizability. Finally, the algorithm is validated through simulations using real-world shipyard transportation data, confirming its practical efficiency and applicability.

records.abstract: Strongly nonlinear multi-field coupling problems in the microwave heating of oil shale require high-precision and efficient solution methods. Physics-informed neural network (PINN) has emerged as a powerful tool for solving partial differential equations (PDEs); however, existing PINN approaches often have limited applicability under specific conditions, and their training convergence remains suboptimal when applied to strongly nonlinear, temperature-dependent material problems. To address this, this study proposes a PINN framework with a strong physical constraint weighting strategy, in which the physical loss weight is constrained within 0.5-0.6 and dynamically balanced during training. Coupled with experimentally obtained temperature-dependent material parameters, this enables efficient surrogate solutions of the coupled PDEs. Three test cases (600 W, 800 W microwave heating, and cross-condition high-temperature steam heating of oil shale) were used for training and prediction. The results show that the PINN framework can output temperature and displacement fields at arbitrary points in milliseconds, with total loss stabilized at the 10^{−4}-10^{−3} level, high prediction accuracy, and strong agreement with COMSOL simulations. These findings demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves high-precision, rapid prediction and cross-condition generalization for strongly nonlinear thermo-mechanical coupling problems in temperature-dependent materials.

records.abstract: Internet of Things environments require secure and privacy-preserving collaborative learning mechanisms that remain robust under emerging quantum-era threats. Many existing distributed learning approaches do not provide dynamic threat detection and quantum-resistant protection, which leaves Internet of Things deployments exposed to adaptive attacks and future cryptanalytic advances. This study proposes an Adaptive Anomaly Detection and Trust-Aware Federated Learning framework to address these limitations. The framework integrates: (i) a deep learning-based adaptive anomaly detection component for real-time identification of malicious behavioral patterns, (ii) a quantitative trust assessment component that computes a mathematical trust score using behavioral evidence, integrity verification outcomes, and time-dependent factors, and (iii) a quantum-resilient encryption mechanism that combines post-quantum cryptography with quantum key distribution while remaining compatible with Internet of Things resource constraints. These components operate within a secure federated learning architecture that employs a decentralized design together with differential privacy and homomorphic encryption to protect local data and secure model aggregation. Experimental evaluation indicates 96% accuracy for anomaly detection, 93% accuracy for trust assessment, 97% encryption stability, and 2–4 s for federation synchronization under the tested settings.

records.abstract: With the rapid advancement of urbanization, structural systems are evolving toward ultra-large-scale and clustered configurations. Correspondingly, the number of degrees of freedom in finite element (FE) models of these large-scale structural systems has increased dramatically, which necessitates efficient computational performance of large-scale sparse linear systems. The preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) method is widely utilized for solving large sparse symmetric positive-definite systems, owing to the preconditioner computational efficiency. This study employs the condition number of the preconditioned matrix as the loss function and develops a sparse convolutional U-shaped neural network (SU-net) as the core architecture for constructing an efficient preconditioner generator. The proposed approach is embedded into the workflow of finite element–based structural analysis, enabling a significant reduction in computational time for displacement responses of superstructure frames and soil–structure interaction systems. Compared with the non-preconditioned CG method, the proposed framework achieves a speedup of 6.23-8.43 times for superstructure frame problems and 13.48-19.89 times for soil–substructure interaction problems, without any loss of accuracy. Furthermore, within the convergence tolerance range of 1 × 10^{−2} to 1 × 10^{−10}, the proposed deep learning-based preconditioner consistently demonstrates superior acceleration in comparison with Jacobi, symmetric Gauss–Seidel, symmetric successive over-relaxation, incomplete Cholesky factorization without fill-in and algebraic multigrid method. The developed SU-net demonstrates strong generalization capability for random material parameter problems at a fixed mesh resolution, suggesting that it has considerable potential as an effective preconditioning strategy for load combination design, material parameter optimization, and stochastic finite element analysis in large-scale structures.

records.abstract: Marine turbochargers are critical for improving fuel efficiency and reducing emissions in maritime transport, yet evaluating their performance under dynamic ocean conditions remains challenging due to incomplete sensor data and limitations of conventional models. While physics-based approaches lack adaptability, purely data-driven methods require complete datasets and may violate thermodynamic consistency. This study proposes a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework that embeds mean - value thermodynamic equations into the loss function, integrating multi-source operational data with physical constraints. The method employs a two-stage progressive training strategy with adaptive weighting and a novel gradient coordination mechanism to balance competing objectives and ensure stable, thermodynamically consistent learning. Validated on 2.1 million data points from a 300,000 DWT bulk carrier, the PINN achieves high accuracy in predicting key turbocharger performance indicators, significantly outperforming traditional models in bench tests and maintaining robust performance even under incomplete parameter conditions. This framework bridges physics-based modeling and deep learning, enabling robust turbocharger evaluation in dynamic environments, advancing condition monitoring, and supporting condition-based maintenance of ship propulsion systems.

records.abstract: Whole-life fatigue crack growth presents a critical challenge in structural integrity assessment, particularly under complex loading conditions. To address the limitations of standard physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in capturing the temporal dynamics of fatigue crack growth, this study proposes an active learning-based physics-informed recurrent neural network (AC-PI-RNN). Specifically, a recurrent neural network (RNN) is integrated with a fully connected network, where dynamic features (stress intensity factor range) and static features (stress ratio, load amplitude, and pre-strain) are fused at the RNN input layer to provide comprehensive loading information. To optimize sample selection under data-limited conditions, a query-by-committee active learning strategy is employed. Furthermore, a modified Jones physical model is embedded into the network's loss function to enforce adherence to the underlying physics of fatigue crack growth. Comprehensive evaluations validate the efficacy of the proposed framework, demonstrating enhanced predictive fidelity, robust generalization, and improved physical consistency. A comparative analysis reveals that the AC-PI-RNN significantly outperforms traditional RNN and PINN models, showing a distinct advantage in capturing the complete trajectory of whole-life crack propagation with high precision. The proposed framework provides an effective and interpretable approach for whole-life fatigue crack growth rate prediction under complex loading conditions.

records.abstract: Knowledge Tracing forecasts students’ future learning outcomes by analyzing historical interactions and modeling learning trajectories, which is essential for personalized learning on online education platforms. However, deep knowledge tracing methods face challenges due to data sparsity, which hinders their ability to differentiate between interactions and leads to overfitting. To address the challenge of data sparsity, this paper proposes a deep knowledge tracing approach that integrates an adversarial contrastive learning framework. This framework generates challenging adversarial samples and uses contrastive learning to refine the model’s discrimination accuracy, helping it learn subtle distinctions between sample categories and improving overall performance. Additionally, our approach incorporates a self-attention mechanism to integrate information from multiple knowledge points, further improving adversarial sample quality through enhanced question embeddings. Experimental results on various real-world educational datasets show that our method significantly outperforms existing methods in prediction accuracy, particularly in datasets with different levels of sparsity, effectively mitigating overfitting. Furthermore, the adversarial contrastive learning framework not only improves the performance of individual models but also demonstrates scalability and flexibility, enabling integration and enhancement of numerous existing knowledge tracing models.

records.abstract: Aiming at the practical problem of visual detection of abnormal surface quality of disposable bamboo chopsticks in an industrial production environment, this paper proposes an application-oriented anomaly detection algorithm based on cross-domain mixup augmentation (CDMA) and self-supervised learning to improve the inspection quality of bamboo chopsticks in production. Firstly, a novel data augmentation algorithm is proposed, which combines cross-domain sample images unrelated to chopsticks images with normal sample images to generate pseudo-abnormal samples and drive model learning. Then, a self-supervised learning algorithm based on intra-class relevance retrieval and reconstruction constraints is proposed. This model reconstructs the normal input images and its associated intra-class image, and at the same time, adds regular term constraints to the pseudo-abnormal images, so that their reconstruction errors could not be lower than a limited value, so as to increase the discrimination with the normal samples. Finally, the maximum local error is used to generate anomaly scores for detection. The experimental results show that the detection accuracy and speed performance of the algorithm have reached an advanced level.

records.abstract: Ultrasound-based liver lesion classification remains challenging because diagnostically relevant cues are often localized, structurally heterogeneous, and easily corrupted by speckle noise, boundary ambiguity, and acquisition variability. Existing deep learning methods mainly emphasize global image-level representations and may therefore be suboptimal for modeling lesion-relevant local morphology. We propose a structure-constrained multi-scale contrastive learning framework for liver ultrasound classification. During training, semantic-guided anchoring is used to identify informative local regions, within which positive samples are selected under joint constraints of semantic similarity, local statistical consistency, and fractal-based structural complexity. A multi-scale local positive mining strategy and multi-positive supervised contrastive objective are further introduced to capture lesion patterns across different spatial granularities and enhance class discrimination. Importantly, the framework requires no auxiliary annotations during inference and operates directly on full ultrasound images. Experiments on a private four-class liver ultrasound dataset and two public ultrasound datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over representative convolutional neural network-based, Transformer-based, self-supervised, and ultrasound-specific methods. On the private dataset, the proposed method achieved 97.27% accuracy, and maintained 91.15% accuracy on an independent external validation cohort. Ablation studies and interpretability analyses further show that the method improves both structural discriminability and lesion-focused attention. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective and practically deployable solution for robust liver lesion classification in ultrasound imaging.

records.abstract: Air pollution from various sources poses a significant threat to human health and the environment. Developing accurate air quality prediction models is crucial for effective environmental monitoring and public health management. Transfer learning has emerged as a promising approach to enhance such models by leveraging knowledge from related domains. This research paper explores the application of homogeneous transfer learning for building more efficient air quality prediction models. By adapting pre-trained models to new air quality datasets, transfer learning improves predictive accuracy, reduces training time, and addresses data scarcity issues. Meteorological and pollutant data from Trivandrum are collected to develop an Air Quality Prediction model. The knowledge from this prebuilt model is then utilized to construct an Air Quality Index (AQI) model for the Cochin region using the deep learning algorithms Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), where data availability is limited. Experimental evaluations on diverse datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of homogeneous transfer learning in enhancing air quality forecasting. The findings highlight the impact of transfer learning in creating robust air quality index models, aiding pollution control and mitigation strategies.

records.abstract: The internal temperature field of a blast furnace, vital for steelmaking, impacts energy use, emissions, and smelting costs, ensuring operational stability. Direct measurement of inner wall temperatures is infeasible due to the furnace’s enclosed, dusty, high-temperature, and high-pressure environment. Current approaches thus rely on sparse outer wall thermocouple measurements to reconstruct the internal temperature field via mathematical models. However, the large furnace volume coupled with limited outer wall data lead to a highly ill-posed inverse heat conduction problem, hindering accuracy and efficiency for industrial needs. To address this, we propose Diffusion-PINN, a Diffusion-Physics-Informed Neural Networks, which transforms the temperature field inversion into a diffusion-based generation process for temperature distribution maps. For the inverse heat conduction problem, the diffusion model is designed to fit the joint distribution of inner and outer wall temperature fields, directly generating coupled temperature distributions to circumvent the multi-solution issue of inverse problems. To address sparse measurement points and enhance solution accuracy, physical heat transfer information is embedded as conditional constraints in the diffusion process, progressively narrowing the constraint range during training. A dynamic loss-pulling algorithm is further proposed to enhance both solution accuracy and training speed. For the challenge of large spatial scales, the computationally intensive inversion process is reduced to a highly parallelizable map generation task, enabling rapid reconstruction of large-scale temperature fields. Simulations demonstrate that this method effectively addresses ill-posed inverse heat conduction problems. When applied to blast furnace smelting, it achieves the accuracy and efficiency required for industrial applications, offering substantial practical value.

records.abstract: Brain tumors present significant neurological challenges with high mortality rates, where early diagnosis based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is clinically vital but is hindered by labor-intensive manual segmentation. To overcome limitations in existing approaches, where convolutional neural networks (CNNs) struggle with global context dependencies and Transformers face computational inefficiency, we propose a dual-branched framework called bifurcated fusion dual-encoder convolutional neural networks –frequency Transformer (BiF-DTNet). The BiF-DTNet employs a dual-encoder architecture, where the CNN encoder captures local features. In contrast, the frequency-domain vision Transformer (FViT) encoder efficiently models global context through fast Fourier transform and self-attention. The model incorporates bidirectional spatial-channel attention (BISC) blocks for effective multi-scale feature fusion, enhancing segmentation accuracy. While BiF-DTNet performs feature encoding on two-dimensional (2D) axial slices for computational efficiency, the model reconstructs the final segmentation in a volumetric manner, enabling precise and coherent three-dimensional (3D) tumor prediction. Evaluated on the brain tumor segmentation (BraTS) 2020 and BraTS 2021 benchmarks, BiF-DTNet achieves Dice scores of 80.42%/85.15%/91.34% (enhancing tumor (ET)/tumor core (TC)/whole tumor (WT)) on BraTS 2020 and 85.98%/91.25%/93.64% on BraTS 2021, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. These results conclusively demonstrate BiF-DTNet’s superiority in precise 3D tumor segmentation, particularly for irregular boundaries and small lesions, through its synergistic integration of local and global features.

records.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is central to brain research and clinical care. However, heterogeneity across scanners, acquisition protocols, and populations, together with privacy constraints, limits the reliability and scalability of the magnetic resonance imaging analysis. In this review, we use brain MRI analysis intelligence (BMI) to denote a layered and governance-aware framework. This framework integrates visual foundation models (VFMs) and federated learning (FL) through shared anatomical representations, lightweight center-local adaptation, and federated orchestration with provenance tracking, privacy budgets, and rollback mechanisms. This review (i) outlines brain magnetic resonance imaging fundamentals and major task categories; (ii) surveys federated learning as a practical route for multi-center collaboration without sharing raw data; and (iii) summarizes visual foundation model pretraining and fine-tuning methods for label-efficient and cross-contrast adaptation. Finally, we summarize three principles toward brain magnetic resonance imaging analysis intelligence: representation first, orchestration always, and measure what matters. Looking ahead, federated visual foundation models, domain adaptation, and governance-aware continual learning could further advance the analysis intelligence toward routinely audited clinical use.

records.abstract: Accurate dynamic modeling of pneumatic actuation systems is crucial for design optimization and control stability. Traditional physics-based models struggle with accuracy and adaptability due to factors like gas compressibility, nonlinear friction, and varying operating conditions, while data-driven models often lack physical consistency and generalize poorly under extrapolated conditions. Although physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) effectively combine physical priors with data-driven learning, existing approaches focus primarily on systems with continuous control inputs, with limited attention given to digitally controlled pneumatic systems using binary on-off valve signals and hybrid dynamics. Furthermore, most PINN methods assume known physical parameters. This paper presents a PINN-based framework for digitally controlled pneumatic systems, directly using binary valve signals as inputs, embedding governing dynamics as soft constraints in the loss function, and introducing a physical-parameter encoder for key constants. An adaptive range-optimization mechanism is also introduced to identify difficult-to-calibrate parameters such as dead volume and friction. Validation of the approach on two pneumatic platforms demonstrates its superiority over purely data-driven feedforward neural networks (FNN) in predicting displacement and pressure, achieving R2 > 0.99 under supply pressure conditions outside the training set. These results confirm the model's accuracy, generalization, and adaptability across diverse operating conditions.

records.abstract: Precipitation nowcasting is a critical field of meteorology research. Current methods fail to fully account for uncertainties in nowcasting, leading to issues such as ambiguity, omission, and localized bias. This paper introduces a conditional diffusion model to mitigate uncertainty by modeling the probability distribution of spatio-temporal evolution features of precipitation. Based on the continuity equation of precipitation evolution, an evolution feature autoencoder decouples the precipitation evolution process into motion fields and precipitation intensity residuals through two distinct encoding pathways. The diffusion model based on U-shaped architecture with spatio-temporal attention mechanism, simulates precipitation evolution conditioned on evolution features. Accurate nowcasting is achieved by decoding the generated spatio-temporal evolution features into precipitation. Extensive experiments on two real-world precipitation datasets demonstrate that the proposed method mitigates uncertainties in nowcasting, particularly for high-intensity precipitation, achieving improvements of at least 10.9% in Critical Success Index (CSI) and and 9.8% in Heidecker Skill Score (HSS) over state-of-the-art methods.

records.abstract: In this study, four artificial intelligence-based time-series foundation models were evaluated: a generative pretrained transformer for time series (TimeGPT), Time Series Foundation Model (TimesFM), Chronos, and Moirai. These models were used to forecast monthly precipitation in four major cities in South Korea: Seoul, Daejeon, Daegu, and Busan. Because of increasing uncertainty in weather forecasts caused by climate change, the development of accurate and efficient prediction models is critical. Historical monthly precipitation data from the Automated Surface Observing System (ASOS), spanning 1985 to 2024, were partitioned into separate training and test sets. We applied a sliding-window approach for continuous model retraining and quantitatively evaluated the prediction accuracy against seasonal autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models. The results highlight the complementary strengths of the time-series foundation models and LSTM baseline relative to the SARIMA benchmark. Moirai was effective in predicting intense, highly variable monsoon rainfall, whereas TimesFM provided stable skill during other, more predictable seasons and surpassed SARIMA in root mean square error (RMSE) for Seoul. The LSTM baseline underperformed in full-period error metrics, but reproduced peak and dry-month precipitation more accurately than the other models, underscoring a tradeoff between average accuracy and fidelity to extremes. SARIMA achieved the lowest full-period RMSE and mean absolute error for most city–lead time combinations. Overall, these findings suggest that combining time-series foundation models with traditional statistical and deep-learning forecasting methods can yield more balanced forecasting performance with lower full-period errors and better capture of extremes.

records.abstract:
Dynamic graph contrastive learning methods commonly assume that nodes preserve stable structural roles over time. However, real-world networks often violate this assumption: nodes may change their connectivity patterns, reactivate after long inactivity, or undergo local structural reorganisation. Such heterogeneity not only weakens temporal consistency constraints but also causes volatile nodes to generate unreliable negative signals. This work shows that temporal contrasts vary substantially in reliability and should not be treated uniformly.

We introduce an uncertainty-aware dynamic graph contrastive learning framework driven by temporal contrast uncertainty, which quantifies the reliability of cross-temporal contrasts directly from the graph structure. Nodes with low temporal contrast uncertainty exhibit stable structural patterns, whereas nodes with high temporal contrast uncertainty indicate volatile evolution. Leveraging temporal contrast uncertainty, the proposed framework integrates three mechanisms: (1) adaptive temporal sampling, (2) uncertainty-weighted contrastive objectives, and (3) group-level prototype calibration to correct estimation bias. We theoretically show that temporal contrast uncertainty weighting yields a favourable trade-off with respect to the mutual information lower bound, while prototype calibration provides an upper bound for controlling temporal drift. Extensive experiments on five benchmark datasets for node classification and seven datasets (including two with real-world anomaly labels) for anomaly detection demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, with pronounced improvements on datasets containing a high proportion of structurally volatile nodes.

records.abstract: Graph anomaly detection has become increasingly crucial for identifying suspicious patterns in complex networks, with broad applications in domains such as social network analysis, fraud detection and network security. Recent advances in graph contrastive learning (GCL) have demonstrated great potential for unsupervised anomaly detection by capturing discriminative representations from local subgraphs. However, existing GCL-based methods still face challenges in detecting subtle anomalies due to the inherent structural heterogeneity of real-world graphs. Furthermore, their reliance on rigid or stochastic subgraph sampling strategies limits their ability to capture fine-grained structural variations, thereby reducing detection sensitivity. To address these limitations, we propose a subgraph-based contrastive learning framework for graph anomaly detection, referred to as SubGAD. Specifically, SubGAD constructs informative subgraph views by integrating first- and second-order neighbors, thereby capturing richer contextual patterns without the bias of fixed-size sampling. It first performs node-to-subgraph contrastive learning to highlight local deviations, and then introduces the Graph Earth Mover’s Distance (G-EMD) to align subgraph representations across views, effectively quantifying structural and semantic discrepancies in a distribution-aware manner. Moreover, SubGAD mitigates positional bias through subgraph centering and performs kernel-based anomaly detection. Extensive experiments on seven real-world datasets demonstrate that SubGAD consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving notable performance gains and confirming its effectiveness in detecting subtle anomalies in attributed graphs. Our source code is available at https://github.com/GNNteam/SubGAD.

records.abstract: Intermittent power (IP) has become an important operational strategy for complex mechatronic systems (CMS) due to its energy-saving potential and dynamic adaptability. However, most existing performance evaluation models assume stable power supply and therefore fail to accurately capture the performance degradation of CMS under IP conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physics-informed belief rule base model with high interpretability for CMS performance evaluation under IP conditions, termed IPBRB-IP. An event-driven damage accumulation model for IP (DAM-IP) is first developed to calculate dynamic damage factors, through explicit embedding of physical knowledge. An interval belief rule base is then constructed, where the bounds of belief distributions are determined conservatively and aggressively using expert knowledge and limited data. Based on the calculated damage factors, the initial belief distributions are adaptively inferred, allowing accurate representation of the performance degradation trajectory of CMS. To further preserve interpretability, an interpretability-constrained optimization criterion is introduced to ensure cognitive consistency between physics-corrected expert understanding and model outputs. Finally, a CMS case study under IP conditions demonstrates the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed approach. From an artificial intelligence perspective, this work develops a physics-informed and interpretable belief rule base framework that integrates damage modeling and knowledge–data fusion for CMS performance evaluation under IP. From an engineering perspective, the proposed IPBRB-IP model provides a transparent and reliable tool for performance evaluation of CMS operating under IP conditions.

records.abstract: Effective thermal management for high-power-density integrated circuits faces significant challenges due to electrical and dimensional constraints in modern electronic systems. Existing design methods often treat thermal analysis as a post-layout verification step, lacking efficient co-optimization strategies. This paper proposes a co-optimization method that integrates data-driven modeling with an adaptive genetic algorithm. First, an electro-thermal coupling model generates a calibrated dataset, enabling the development of a high-precision chip temperature predictor using the extreme gradient boosting algorithm. The proposed model then optimizes printed circuit board layout parameters under simultaneous electrical and dimensional constraints. The integrated extreme gradient boosting based adaptive genetic algorithm demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional models, achieving an average temperature reduction of 2.92% over the standard genetic algorithm and 4.93% over Bayesian optimization. Subsequent simulations and experimental validations confirm the accuracy of steady-state temperature predictions. Experimental findings reveal that, across varying load conditions, the optimized samples exhibit an average target temperature reduction of 7.95%, with a maximum decrease of 8.54 °C. These results demonstrate its practical value of the proposed model, providing an optimization strategy for thermal design of high-power-density integrated circuits.
