records.abstract: Heavy metal contamination in industrial wastewater requires sustainable remediation solutions. This study introduces a hybrid computational framework combining Fractional-Order Physics-Informed Neural Networks (FO-PINNs) for surrogate modeling, Reinforcement Learning (RL) for dynamic optimization, and blockchain for auditable logging, applied to Direct Contact Membrane Distillation (DCMD). Under CFD-verified simulation conditions over a 12-h cycle (1500 epochs), the framework predicts a mean permeate flux of 4.51 L/m^{2}.h, representing a 32% improvement compared to non-foam CFD baselines, and suggests a 68% reduction in fouling rate. Energy-intensity modeling, after subtracting computational overhead, indicates an approximate 15% net reduction in CO_{2} emissions under the simulated operating conditions. Blockchain provides auditable data tracking, while a GUI facilitates dynamic optimization. While experimental validation remains necessary, this approach demonstrates the feasibility of physics-informed adaptive control for DCMD and offers a foundation for scalable, low-carbon wastewater treatment.

records.abstract: Optical communication systems require compact routing elements that maintain high transmission while minimizing bending loss. This study presents an artificial-intelligence-assisted inverse-design framework based on a multilayer perceptron neural network to optimize a two-dimensional photonic crystal waveguide incorporating a 90-degree bend for broadband telecommunication operation. First, three candidate bend configurations were evaluated using full-wave electromagnetic simulations, and the third configuration provided the best conventional performance, achieving a maximum bandwidth of 165.1 nm with a minimum transmission loss of 11.76 percent, including 73.1 nm within the original telecommunication band. Next, the multilayer perceptron neural network was trained on simulated samples incorporating waveguide operating conditions, enabling rapid prediction of improved geometric parameters. The waveguide predicted by the neural network was then re-simulated, demonstrating a 26.288 percent increase in bandwidth to 208.5 nm. In this case, the proposed waveguide completely covered the original telecommunications band and 50.6 nm of the telecommunications Extended-band. Across the entire operating bandwidth, transmission losses remained below 10 percent, and at the peak bandwidth, they were below 1.2 percent, representing an 89.8 percent reduction compared to the previous best case. These results show that neural network-based inverse design can efficiently identify parameter settings that substantially improve bandwidth and reduce loss in photonic crystal waveguide bends, providing a practical route toward data-driven design of photonic integrated circuits.

records.abstract: In this study, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework was proposed for predicting hydrogen production in the gasification of plastic waste by embedding kinetic- and equilibrium-based physical knowledge as soft constraints into the learning process. Three PINN variants—kinetic, equilibrium, and combined—were developed and compared with a conventional artificial neural network (ANN) under varying dataset ratios (1%, 10%, 50%, and 100%) to evaluate their performance in data-scarce environments. Although the ANN model exhibited substantial performance degradation with limited data, all PINN models maintained robust predictive accuracy (R^{2}, the coefficient of determination >0.99) and physically plausible behavior within the surrogate modeling scope, with the equilibrium model achieving the lowest error and the combined model showing the best overall balance. Gradient-based residual analysis also confirmed that the PINN results were consistent with expected thermodynamic and reaction trends, rather than strictly enforcing the governing physical laws. Although the models were trained on simulated data from a simplified single-unit process, they have demonstrated their effectiveness as a proof-of-concept for physics-guided surrogate modeling, providing a useful basis for future real-time optimization and control of hydrogen production systems.

records.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a deep learning framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs). However, standard approaches often struggle to strictly enforce boundary conditions, limiting their computational accuracy, especially in complex multiphysics coupled systems. To address this challenge, we introduce Boundary Region Reinforcement Physics-Informed Neural Networks (BRR-PINNs), a novel framework designed to strengthen boundary constraint enforcement and significantly improve solution accuracy. The method converts non-Dirichlet conditions into exact Dirichlet boundaries using intermediate variables to reduce redundant loss terms, and applies a spatial reinforcement function to prioritize training near boundaries. We validate the effectiveness of BRR-PINNs on a two-dimensional axisymmetric thermo-elastic coupling problem, involving a circular ring subjected to both thermal and mechanical loads. Experimental results show that our method consistently outperforms several existing approaches, achieving approximately one order of magnitude improvement in accuracy.

records.abstract: High-resolution hyperspectral images enable precise fragment detection, explosive residue analysis, and explosion-proof design. Owing to technical restrictions in hyperspectral sensor hardware, significant challenges exist in acquiring high-resolution hyperspectral images of small-sized fragments at a safe standoff distance. Hyperspectral image super-resolution (HISR) technology can compensate for the limitations of single-sensor imaging, enabling the simultaneous acquisition of spatial details and spectral information of fragments. However, most existing super-resolution networks are trained on simulated degraded image pairs, failing to account for the issue of spatial misalignment between heterogeneous sensors. Therefore, a mathematical observation model is developed to describe the physical degradation during the fusion of fragment low-resolution hyperspectral images and high-resolution Red-Green-Blue (RGB) images, considering the presence of spatial misalignment. Based on these models, we then propose a fragment target-based unsupervised transformer-enhanced deep image prior network (FT-UTDIP-Net) for selected-band HISR. The network comprises modules for image registration and blur kernel learning, initial image estimation generation, multi-scale feature progressive alignment, and super resolution hyperspectral image generation. The proposed method achieves promising fusion performance for HISR across both public and selected-band steel fragment datasets. Furthermore, downstream experiments demonstrate that the method significantly enhances fragment recognition performance. This study demonstrates feasibility for selected-band HISR of steel fragments under a controlled UAV acquisition setting.

records.abstract: In laser welding, the penetration state is a critical factor affecting joint formation quality and service performance. However, during actual welding processes, the molten pool exhibits a delayed response to heat input, and the welding system inherently involves unavoidable delays, which significantly limit the effectiveness of traditional real-time monitoring and control methods. To address these issues, this research proposes a laser welding molten pool state ahead prediction method that integrates physics features based on dimensionless numbers, aiming to mitigate delay effects in the welding process and to provide predictive state information for intelligent welding process control. The proposed method exploits image sequences to characterize the dynamic behaviors of the molten pool and keyhole. By analyzing the thermal history characteristics of the welding process, a penetration state score model is introduced, providing a physical motivation for modeling temporal dependencies. On this basis, dimensionless number-based physics features are collaboratively integrated with image sequences, leading to the development of a physics-informed multi-scale temporal convolutional network (MSP-TCN). The proposed model is capable of learning the evolution patterns of the molten pool state across different welding scenarios in a more stable manner, thereby enabling ahead prediction of molten pool state sequences. Experimental validation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms purely image-driven models in terms of both prediction accuracy and generalization capability, providing an effective solution for delay compensation in laser welding processes.

records.abstract: Most flow-induced vibration (FIV) studies rely on amplitude or correlations without quantifying causal paths. We introduce a physics-informed causal inference framework to explain heat transfer mechanisms. A directed acyclic graph was pre-specified from fluid–structure–thermal interaction principles and evaluated using mediation analysis of 120 high-fidelity simulations covering Re = 2300–7700, Ur = 5–15, and G = 0.4–1.2. The optimal spectral-response regime achieved a peak performance evaluation criterion (PEC) of 1.32 ± 0.03 (sampling error; combined uncertainty ±0.06), exceeding the energy-efficiency threshold of PEC = 1.0, while excessive structural stiffness reduced PEC by 18.3%. Three dominant causal pathways were statistically validated, with path coefficients of |β| = 0.25–0.38 (bootstrap 95% CIs excluding zero) (p < 0.001). Compared with an amplitude-only benchmark, spectral features explained an additional 18.3% of performance variance and mediated 63–64% of the total causal effect from system parameters to performance, demonstrating that vibration quality is not a secondary descriptor but a primary causal determinant. Physically, high Spectral Purity enabled vortex–thermal phase locking with Δt/T = 0.12 ± 0.02, Harmonic Energy Ratio predicted regime transitions with 87% accuracy and a 6% false-positive rate, and high Modal Coherence directed 72% of vibrational energy into productive thermal mixing, compared with only 38% in low-coherence configurations. Bootstrap resampling confirmed that the identified causal pathways remained directionally consistent in more than 96% of resamples. The present framework lies not only in predicting enhanced heat transfer but also in explaining why it occurs, thereby shifting FIV thermal-system design from amplitude maximization toward spectral-quality optimization.

records.abstract:
Parametric analysis of discrete engineering structures requires repeated finite element simulations, leading to high computational cost in design exploration. Graph neural operators have emerged as a promising surrogate modeling framework for learning parametric solution mappings on graph-structured systems; however, existing approaches remain limited in effectively capturing long-range dependencies.

This study introduces an attention-based graph neural operator (AGNO) for learning parametric response mappings in discrete structural systems under variations in node-indexed features, particularly structural geometry (via nodal coordinates) and applied nodal loading. The proposed model integrates kernel-induced graph neural operator layers, which emulate operator learning through edge-conditioned message passing, with a permutation-invariant global attention mechanism acting on graph-indexed latent functions, resulting in a unified local–global operator architecture.

The key contribution lies in addressing the locality of graph neural operators in the context of discrete structural systems through this local–global operator architecture. This formulation enables effective modeling of nonlocal structural interactions while preserving topology-aware local behavior, and provides a principled operator-learning framework tailored to graph-based structural response problems.

The approach is evaluated on benchmark problems involving two- and three-dimensional trusses and frames, including mesh-refinement studies and scaling to larger structural systems. Results show that AGNO demonstrates strong performance compared to existing graph-based and operator-learning surrogate models across the considered benchmarks, achieving lower prediction errors and improved robustness with respect to discretization refinement and increasing geometric complexity, while maintaining comparable computational cost. These findings indicate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for parametric response prediction in discrete structural systems under the tested conditions.

records.abstract: Generative models have become a foundational technology for medical imaging, supporting image generation, enhancement, segmentation, registration, image-to-image translation, and anomaly detection. Despite the rapid growth of methodological work, the literature still lacks a unified comparative framework that helps practitioners decide between Generative Adversarial Networks, Variational Autoencoders, and diffusion models for specific medical-imaging tasks; existing surveys also provide limited treatment of validation strategies, dataset constraints, and ethical or clinical considerations. This survey reviews representative methods from each model family across six core tasks, covering anomaly detection, image-to-image translation, image generation, segmentation, denoising, and registration, consolidating them into a unified comparison spanning accuracy, computational cost, data requirements, robustness, uncertainty quantification, and practical deployment. We further compile commonly used benchmark datasets together with their scale, diversity, and known limitations, and we critically discuss validation strategies, model complexity and regularization, and ethical, clinical, and practical considerations. Our key findings are threefold. First, no single model family dominates across all tasks, as Generative Adversarial Networks remain leading for image-to-image translation and data augmentation, Variational Autoencoders are well-suited to reconstruction-based anomaly detection where their posterior provides native uncertainty estimates, and diffusion models currently offer the strongest results in image generation, segmentation, and denoising. Second, practical deployment metrics and external validation remain under-reported in the literature, which limits clinical translation. Third, domain shift, demographic bias, regulatory uncertainty, and reproducibility are open challenges shared across model families. We close with a conceptual taxonomy organized along the model-family by imaging-task axis and outline future research directions.

records.abstract: The fast development of electric vehicles is putting a strain on the possibility of having intelligent bidirectional charging infrastructures, which are capable of supporting vehicle to grid operation but are also able to handle renewable intermittency and rapid load swings. The current energy management and control policies of renewable-integrated charging stations frequently cannot be used to guarantee high power quality, real-time feasibility, and robust stability at the same time, especially when sophisticated storage technology is used. This paper develops a unified control and artificial intelligence solution to bidirectional electric vehicle charging which integrates superconducting magnetic energy storage with solar photovoltaic and wind generation. A barrier based super-twisting sliding mode controller is designed at the control level to impose safety requirements, enhance disturbance rejection, and reduce chattering with parameter uncertainty. Red Fox Optimization aims at optimizing controller gains with the view of improving dynamic performance. Bidirectional recurrent neural networks at the intelligence layer forecast renewable power, and a Deep Q-Network based reinforcement learning energy management system optimizes and determines the best power scheduling between the grid, renewable sources, electric vehicle battery and superconducting magnetic storage. In addition, performance of the proposed super-twisting sliding mode controller with enhanced barrier functionality is compared to a synergetic approach to control and confirmed in a high-fidelity hardware-in-the-loop experiment. High-fidelity simulations and experimental validation demonstrate improved charging efficiency, enhanced utilization of superconducting magnetic energy storage during fast transients, and reduced total harmonic distortion during transitions between grid-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-grid modes. The proposed framework offers a scalable and intelligent solution for renewable-aware bidirectional charging in sustainable transportation systems.

records.abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting (WPF) is crucial for ensuring the stable operation of power systems. Long-term effective forecasting can optimize wind power generation planning and reduce operational costs. Although deep learning advancements have significantly improved wind power forecasting accuracy, existing methods often struggle to effectively separate the complex relationships between variables, features, and time dimensions in multivariate time-series data, limiting their predictive performance. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel model, named Triple Decoupled Transformer (TDFormer), for multi-step wind power forecasting. The model incorporates a novel Triple Decoupled Attention (TDA) mechanism to independently decouple input data across three dimensions—variables, features, and time—enabling more efficient and precise feature extraction. TDFormer adopts an encoder-decoder architecture to integrate historical data from multiple variables and future time sequences, making it ideal for multi-step wind power forecasting. Extensive experiments conducted on real-world datasets from wind farms with varying capacities and geographical locations demonstrate that the proposed TDFormer significantly outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, especially in scenarios involving longer forecasting horizons. In addition, the model demonstrated excellent generalization ability and practical application potential in the transfer learning experiments, making it particularly suitable for newly established wind farms with limited data, and offering significant application value. The source code and datasets are available at https://github.com/USTC-AI4EEE/TDFormer.

records.abstract: Deep learning has become increasingly important in seismic monitoring and analysis, yet most existing methods remain heavily dependent on large labeled datasets and often transfer poorly across tasks and regions. To address these limitations, this study proposes ConProSeis, a self-supervised pretraining framework for learning transferable representations from seismic waveforms. ConProSeis develops a prototype-driven contrastive strategy that uses diverse physics-guided multi-view augmentations to improve representation robustness and reduce semantic shifts caused by perturbations. Intra-prototype and inter-prototype contrastive losses are further introduced to enhance feature discrimination. A dual-encoder architecture is adopted, in which the target encoder is updated by exponential moving average to stabilize training. Experiments on a large-scale Chinese seismic dataset show that the learned representations transfer effectively to earthquake event classification, magnitude regression, and phase detection. In tectonic-versus-non-tectonic event classification, ConProSeis achieves an accuracy of 99.03%. Additional experiments on the Pacific Northwest dataset further demonstrate cross-regional transferability. Overall, the results suggest that physics-aware self-supervised pretraining can reduce label dependence and improve the robustness and transferability of seismic representation learning.

records.abstract: Reinforced concrete (RC) chimneys represent critical industrial infrastructure with significant seismic vulnerability due to their slender and high-rise geometry. Conventional nonlinear numerical simulations, while accurate, are computationally expensive and unsuitable for real-time response prediction and large-scale parametric investigations. This study addresses these limitations by proposing a Deep Learning (DL) framework for fast and accurate prediction of dynamic seismic responses. A dataset of over 40,000 high-fidelity Nonlinear Time History Analyses (NLTHAs) was generated using OpenSees, incorporating diverse geometric configurations, and material nonlinearities subjected to real Ground Motion Acceleration (GMA) records scaled across multiple intensities. A hybrid Transformer-based architecture is proposed, utilizing a multi-task learning configuration with a shared encoder backbone, a transfer learning strategy and an adaptive sequence compression module. This design allows the model to simultaneously predict dominant modal frequencies and full dynamic response time histories, while effectively managing long-range temporal dependencies. The model demonstrates exceptional predictive accuracy on unseen test data, achieving Pearson correlation coefficients (R) exceeding 0.99 for modal frequencies and 0.98 for dynamic response time histories. It demonstrates promising generalization capability for previously unseen geometries and seismic waveforms, maintaining high fidelity in capturing peak responses, and phase alignment. The architecture reduces computational cost from several minutes per simulation to milliseconds per prediction. This efficiency enables near-instantaneous predictions, providing a practical tool for performance-based design and potential future integration into real-time structural health monitoring of critical industrial infrastructure.

records.abstract: State-of-health (SOH) estimation is critical for ensuring the safe and reliable operation of lithium-ion batteries. However, limited data and insufficient temporal–spatial feature representation often restrict model performance. To address these challenges, we propose a novel SOH estimation method that integrates data augmentation, temporal modeling, and feature attention mechanisms. First, a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) is employed to generate multidimensional temporal health features of batteries, which can improve both the quantity and diversity of training data. Subsequently, a self-learning dynamic channel attention (SDCA) mechanism is designed to adaptively model the correlations among cross-channel features via dynamic convolution kernels, enabling the model to focus on more informative features during prediction. Finally, an SOH estimation framework named SDCA-assisted extended long short-term memory network (SDCA-xLSTM) is developed, which adopts the extended long short-term memory (xLSTM) to better capture long-term dependencies in sequential data. Experiments on two battery datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior SOH estimation performance, outperforming several state-of-the-art baselines.

records.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables the simultaneous capture of gene expression profiles and spatial localization, offering critical insights that facilitate the deciphering of tissue architecture and cell–cell interactions. To fully exploit spatial transcriptomic data, effective modeling of spatial relationships is essential. However, current methods exhibit limitations when constructing graph structures. Traditional static topological relationships built on spatial proximity struggle to delineate cell-layer boundaries and fail to adequately identify the cross-regional distribution patterns of cells within the same layer. Meanwhile, those based on raw gene expression similarity are susceptible to noise and cellular heterogeneity, making it difficult to capture the underlying semantic relationships. To address these challenges, we propose GTFST, a graph–Transformer network for spatial transcriptomics clustering. GTFST employs a dual-branch architecture with designed Reciprocal Contrastive Alignment (RCA) strategy to comprehensively model both local microenvironmental interactions and global contextual semantics. Notably, we introduce a Semantic Graph Induction (SGI) module that automatically learns and induces graph topology from gene semantic relationships. This design overcomes the limitations of fixed-neighborhood approaches, enabling more insightful modeling of complex biological interactions. Extensive experiments on spatial transcriptomic datasets demonstrate the superiority of GTFST over state-of-the-art methods in spatial domain clustering. Its enhanced precision provides a robust foundation for subsequent biological analyses such as differentially expressed gene identification, functional enrichment, and cell–cell interaction inference.

records.abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that significantly affects human motor functions, particularly gait patterns. Early and accurate diagnosis of PD is essential for timely clinical intervention. However, manual diagnosis based on visual observation of gait can be time-consuming and error-prone. To achieve faster and more accurate diagnosis, this article presents a combination of Faster region-convolutional neural network (R-CNN) and convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) based artificial intelligence (AI) system to diagnose PD by analyzing the human gait from the videos. In the proposed framework, Faster R-CNN with a residual network 50 (ResNet50) backbone has been used to detect and extract the human subject from each video frame, enabling robust person localization under varying backgrounds and lighting conditions. Subsequently, spatial gait features have been extracted from the detected human using convolutional layers. The extracted frame-level features have been aggregated to form a sequence representing the entire video. These sequential features have been provided to a bidirectional long short-term memory (BLSTM) network to model temporal dependencies across frames and predict the final class label of the video. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves classification accuracies of 91.85%, 99.30%, 99.70%, and 97.82% on four popular publicly available datasets knee osteoarthritis-Parkinson’s disease-normal (KOA-PD-NM), gait-Instituto Superior Tecnico (IST), gait-Instituto de Telecomunicacoes (IT), and multimodal video dataset respectively, outperforming several state-of-the-art gait-based PD diagnosis methods. These results indicate that integrating robust human detection with spatio-temporal deep learning improves PD diagnosis from gait videos and shows strong potential for real-world clinical screening.

records.abstract: Early cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk assessment based on pulse wave analysis is challenged by data scarcity, severe class imbalance, and the difficulty of modeling continuous pathological progression with discrete classification schemes. To learn data distributions from limited samples and to generate high-fidelity synthetic pulse waves for data augmentation, this study proposes a Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) enhanced one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) framework for pulse-wave-based CVD risk grading. Subjects are stratified into four clinically meaningful stages—healthy controls, risk exposure, sub-clinical damage, and confirmed lesion—based on vascular functional and structural indicators, enabling a physiologically interpretable pathological continuum. The proposed framework demonstrates strong classification performance under extreme class imbalance. By augmenting limited real pulse-wave samples into a substantially larger training set, the framework achieved an overall accuracy of 92.28% and a recall of 85.33% for severe lesion cases, representing improvements of 8.54% and 24.00%, respectively, compared with the baseline model trained on the original unaugmented dataset. Moreover, the framework may also be beneficial in scenarios with relatively sufficient data, where generative augmentation can further enrich feature variation and potentially improve classification performance. These results indicate that the proposed method provides a robust and generalizable engineering solution for early CVD risk screening.

records.abstract: Accurate short-term forecasting of photovoltaic power generation is a critical enabler for reliable microgrid operation. However, forecasting accuracy is frequently hindered by data non-stationarity, regime-dependent variability, and the presence of non-physical records within operational datasets. To address these challenges, this study develops a volatility-aware gating, adaptive hybrid forecasting framework using two years of hourly measurements collected from the Datan Power Plant. A physics-informed data validation procedure is applied to improve data quality by excluding nighttime samples according to the solar zenith angle. The proposed architecture employs a shared convolutional neural network-bidirectional long short-term memory backbone for temporal feature extraction and integrates a dual-branch architecture designed to capture both stable and volatile regimes. These branches are interconnected through a sigmoid-based gating mechanism that adaptively blends a dense-fusion stable branch with an attention-enhanced volatile branch in response to input variability. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms the naive baseline, achieving reductions in mean absolute error, weighted mean relative error, root mean square error, and mean absolute percentage error by 18.27%, 20.84%, 23.83%, and 23.86%, respectively. These findings underscore the robustness of the adaptive hybrid model in handling volatile photovoltaic generation patterns and emphasize its potential to improve forecasting reliability in microgrid systems incorporating renewable energy sources.

records.abstract: Predicting the transient temperature field of three-dimensional (3D) targets under rapidly changing weather remains challenging due to the prohibitive cost of traditional solvers, the training instability of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), and the poor generalization of data-driven methods. This paper addresses all three challenges through a unified Parameterized-Hard-Constrained PINN (P-HC-PINN) framework with three key innovations. First, a hard-constrained PINN (HC-PINN) enforces initial conditions exactly, yielding stable training and partial differential equation (PDE) loss of 2.9e-5, three orders of magnitude lower than a soft-constrained baseline. Second, extending this to a Parameterized HC-PINN (P-HC-PINN) that accepts meteorological parameters as inputs enables prediction for new conditions 200 times faster than retraining the HC-PINN. Third, the physics of rain is integrated into the loss function, reducing the rain-period prediction error by 64%. Validated on experimental and simulated data, the framework predicts full-day 3D temperature fields of thin-walled targets with a mean error below 2 K and inference speeds 100 times faster than finite-volume simulations, providing a fast, physics-aware, and generalizable surrogate for thermal analysis.

records.abstract: Pipeline transportation is essential for high-pressure gas delivery, but leaks cause significant economic and environmental damage. Traditional localization methods, which rely on external monitoring or dense sensor networks, are limited in harsh marine environments. This study proposes a pipeline leakage localization framework using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), which reconstructs internal flow fields from sparse sensor data and extracts physically interpretable indicators for detection. Three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were performed to generate leakage flow-field data under various conditions (0.5–2 MPa pressure, different leak locations and angles, and single/dual leakage scenarios). So the optimal sensor configuration was identified as five monitoring planes with four sensors on each plane. The PINN embeds Navier-Stokes and continuity equations into the loss function, reconstructing the entire flow field using only 20 sensors. Leakage localization is achieved by analyzing axial velocity profiles and applying a threshold indicator. For single-leakage cases, the average localization error is approximately 7.5% over all tested conditions, with larger errors in some high-pressure cases with large polar-angle offsets. For dual-leakage cases, the errors are mainly within 2%–13%. This approach enables high-precision leakage localization with low sensor density, offering a feasible solution for intelligent pipeline monitoring in complex environments.

records.abstract: Groundwater is a critical freshwater resource worldwide, yet its sustainability is increasingly threatened by over-extraction and climate variability. Accordingly, reliable and computationally efficient forecasting of groundwater is essential for supporting adaptive aquifer management. In this regard, this study develops a Spatio-Temporal Feature Mixer (STFMixer) deep learning model to forecast groundwater hydraulic heads three months ahead in the Choushui River Alluvial Fan, a region strongly influenced by agricultural pumping and climatic variability in Central Taiwan. The STFMixer model integrates convolutional spatio-temporal encoding with temporal and feature mixing layers to jointly learn spatial, temporal, and inter-feature dependencies of groundwater changes based on historical five-month inputs, including hydraulic heads from groundwater monitoring wells interpolated to spatial grids, gridded precipitation and temperature, and spatially aggregated pumping electricity consumption. Predictive performance is benchmarked against four established deep learning architectures: Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM), Time-Series Mixer (TSMixer), Transformer, and Convolutional Neural Network-Backpropagation Neural Network (CNN-BPNN) models under identical calibration conditions (2007-2017 training; 2018-2021 testing). Results showed that STFMixer achieved the highest average Index of Agreement (IOA >0.79) and lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE <1.5 m) among the evaluated models, while maintaining stable error growth in three-month-ahead forecasting at a spatially heterogeneous aquifer. Ablation analysis further indicated that pumping input contributes most strongly to predictive performance, followed by precipitation and temperature which is typically observed for agriculturally active regions. With approximately 224 thousand trainable parameters which is significantly lower than most benchmark models, the proposed STFMixer model provides a computationally efficient framework for short-term multi-step groundwater forecasting and aquifer management.

records.abstract: To address the computational bottleneck of deep learning, a key artificial intelligence (AI) technology, in resource-constrained Battery Management Systems (BMS), this paper presents a lightweight, linear-complexity State of Health (SOH) estimation framework. First, a systematic feature selection process identifies robust health indicators from partial voltage–time integrals, effectively reducing online extraction burdens. Subsequently, we propose SL-AgentNet (integrating Small-kernel and Large-kernel convolutions), an AI architecture designed to resolve the quadratic overhead of traditional Transformers. By integrating the Fast Local–Global Fusion Attention (FLFA) mechanism with diversity-enhancing modules, specifically the Fast Diversity Feature Fusion Attention (FDFA) and Parallel Informed Activation Function (PIAF), this AI model achieves linear complexity while capturing long-range degradation dependencies. Experiments on the Oxford, National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), and Center for Advanced Life Cycle Engineering (CALCE) datasets demonstrate superior robustness, reducing the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 74.78% on the Oxford dataset against Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-Transformer baselines. With a model size of only 40.92 Kilobytes (KB), the AI framework proves its feasibility through hardware-in-the-loop validation on a Texas Instruments (TI) Cortex-M4 microcontroller, where a Look-Up Table (LUT) implementation maintains accuracy loss within 0.3%, demonstrating its readiness for embedded deployment.

records.abstract: Intelligent monitoring at underground drilling sites underpins mine automation, where rapid and accurate object detection is essential for both production efficiency and safety. However, drilling-site imagery is shaped by multiple factors, including non-uniform illumination, cluttered equipment, and frequent viewpoint changes, resulting in large appearance and scale variations that are difficult to handle with standard detectors. To address these challenges, we propose an Efficient Hybrid Detection Network (EHD-Net) for high-accuracy detector for drilling-site surveillance. Specifically, our backbone adopts the Large–Small Kernel Block (LSKB) to expand the receptive field while preserving local details. We introduce a Shallow–Deep Interaction Attention (SDIA) to couple shallow-detail features with deeper semantic representations. For scale variation, we design an efficient Multi-Scale Fusion Block (MSFB) with lateral residual connections between parallel branches. In addition, a Channel-Spatial Gated Unit (CSGU) is applied along the backbone–neck pathway to suppress irrelevant activations. We further collect a dataset of 17,358 real-world drilling-site images from four coal mines in Henan Province. On the proposed drilling-site dataset, EHD-Net achieves 92.1% mean average precision (mAP) at an inference speed of 123 frames per second (FPS). The corresponding precision and recall are 94.4% and 88.5%, respectively. It also generalizes well to public coal mine benchmarks, including safety helmet and conveyor belt datasets, demonstrating strong cross scenario performance in underground environments.

records.abstract: Accurate characterization of mechanical fields under load is essential for material assessment and engineering design. Although Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are powerful for solving inverse problems, they typically rely on noisy, pre-processed Digital Image Correlation (DIC) data, which can lead to significant error propagation. This paper proposes an image-driven physics-informed neural network (I-PINN), a unified framework that fundamentally overcomes this limitation by integrating full-field image data into the learning process. Instead of relying on discrete DIC-derived points, the method introduces a dense observational constraint based on brightness constancy at the original signal level. Combined with equilibrium residuals, boundary conditions, and a global energy balance, the I-PINN framework enables solving the forward and inverse problems simultaneously without intermediate error propagation steps. Furthermore, a two-stage training strategy is implemented to ensure convergence by learning data-consistent kinematics prior to enforcing physical constraints. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed framework yields physically consistent and accurate displacement, strain, and stress fields and reliably identifies material parameters, even with poor initial guesses. The approach outperforms traditional DIC-based analysis and delivers comparable accuracy to finite element analysis. Ablation studies further confirm the essential roles of the dense image-based constraint and the adopted training strategy for robust convergence. Noise robustness experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach maintains stable reconstruction accuracy and reliable parameter identification even under significant image noise. Overall, the proposed methodology establishes a noise-resistant framework that directly bridges experimental observations and mechanical field inference, offering an effective solution for mechanical field reconstruction and material identification.

records.abstract: Cyanobacteria Harmful Algal Blooms (CyanoHABs) in inland water reservoirs pose ecological and public health risks. Unlike previous studies that primarily focused on past bloom detection, this research introduces a novel framework that predicts future CyanoHAB coverage under climate change scenarios using meteorological variables. Specifically, satellite remote sensing is integrated with hybrid machine learning and deep learning models to detect and project CyanoHAB coverage in Oman's largest reservoir, the Wadi Dayqah Dam. Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) and Landsat satellite images (2010–2023) were utilized to estimate bloom area sizes via the Floating Algae Index (FAI), achieving strong validation. We evaluated four models: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Random Forest combined with LSTM (RF + LSTM), Extreme Gradient Boosting combined with LSTM (XGBoost + LSTM), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine combined with LSTM (LGBoost + LSTM). The best performing model was RF + LSTM. Temperature was identified through sensitivity analysis as the most significant bloom driver. Projections using downscaled Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) data revealed opposite trends: in Shared Socioeconomic Pathway 126 (SSP126), bloom coverage decreased by the late century, particularly in spring (March averages <0.1 square kilometers); Shared Socioeconomic Pathway 245 (SSP245) stayed near historical levels; while Shared Socioeconomic Pathway 585 (SSP585) increased bloom coverage, with summer maxima >0.7 square kilometers. Hybrid modeling effectively predicts CyanoHABs, with temperature as the main driver, and climate mitigation can help reduce associated risks. The findings support adaptive water management and bloom preparedness, noting that larger bloom coverage generally signals higher ecological and public health concerns.

records.abstract: Decomposition methods, such as complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN), effectively address the non-stationary and intermittent nature of time series in wind power and wind speed forecasting, enhancing prediction accuracy. However, the residual noise in the subsequences generated by these decomposition methods can degrade predictive performance. Furthermore, most existing predictive models rarely address the reduction of redundant nonlinear operations in the neuron activation functions within the regression subnetwork, which can lead to high computational costs and diminished prediction accuracy. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel decomposition-based deep stacked residual convolutional recurrent neural network (DB-DSRC-RNN) for wind speed and wind power forecasting. DB-DSRC-RNN first uses CEEMDAN to decompose non-stationary wind speed or power data into stable subsequences. Then, a deep stacked residual convolutional recurrent neural network (DSRC-RNN) learns the underlying spatio-temporal features in each subsequence. In DSRC-RNN, a residual convolution threshold denoising block is designed to mitigate the impact of residual noise in the subsequences of CEEMDAN for the first time, while extracting spatial features. A bidirectional long short-term memory is also integrated into DSRC-RNN to capture temporal features. Additionally, a regression subnetwork with a dense dendrite module is designed to further enhance the model’s performance by reducing the computational complexity associated with nonlinear activation functions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed DB-DSRC-RNN outperforms eight benchmark models in terms of predictive accuracy, generalization ability, and robustness for ultra-short-term wind power and wind speed forecasting in energy systems.

records.abstract: Traditional empirical formulas suffer from insufficient accuracy and limited applicability in predicting the seismic performance of reinforced concrete (RC) columns, while high-precision machine learning (ML) models are often inapplicable in engineering practice due to their “black-box” nature. These issues constitute two core challenges in the field of seismic assessment for reinforced concrete columns. To address these challenges, this study proposes an integrated method combining two-stage machine learning prediction, interpretable analysis, and explicit formula derivation, aiming to simultaneously enhance prediction accuracy, improve model transparency, and derive an explicit formula for practical engineering use. The study achieves this by proposing a novel “classify-then-regress” strategy which first predicts the failure mode and then uses the predicted failure-mode information to condition the Categorical feature boosting (CatBoost)-based shear capacity prediction. The resulting two-stage model achieves high predictive accuracy while providing an explicit failure-mode-conditioned pathway for engineering interpretation and safety-oriented assessment. To tackle the “black-box” issue, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantifies the non-linear effects of key parameters and reveals the model's physical logic, leading to an explicit formula with clear physical meaning. While slightly less accurate than the full machine learning model, this formula significantly surpasses traditional formulas and compensates for the lack of interpretability in data-driven methods. Finally, a graphical user interface (GUI) is developed to integrate the system, providing engineers with an efficient and intuitive tool for practical seismic assessment.

records.abstract: Reconnaissance Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) operating in complex adversarial electromagnetic environments are highly vulnerable to dynamic jamming. To address this challenge, we formulate the UAV’s jamming-resilient maneuvering problem as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP), integrating flight dynamics with physical-layer receiver performance. However, solving this POMDP requires accurately estimating the underlying continuous and time-varying jamming dynamics from only discrete, noisy observations. Standard recurrent networks often fall short because they fail to explicitly model the physical process governing jamming evolution. Our key insight is that jamming dynamics, despite being observed discretely, evolve continuously over time. To bridge this gap, we introduce a novel physical perception encoder that integrates Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) with Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) solvers. The GRU efficiently extracts latent features from historical observation sequences, while the ODE solver serves as a continuous-time dynamics engine, interpolating and extrapolating these latent states to simulate jammer behavior between and beyond observation points. This GRU-ODE encoder is embedded within a Discrete Soft Actor-Critic (DSAC) framework, forming an end-to-end intelligent decision-maker. The resulting algorithm, DSAC-ODE, synergistically optimizes both low-power reconnaissance modes—achieved through sampling bit truncation and beam sparse control—and adaptive flight maneuvers to balance mission success against energy consumption. Extensive evaluations demonstrate its superior performance: a 97% mission success rate, an average decision delay of just 47 ms, and a 9.25% reduction in energy consumption, outperforming several strong baselines.

records.abstract: The accurate and concurrent estimation of a lithium-ion battery's electrochemical impedance spectrum (EIS), state of charge (SOC), and state of health (SOH) is critical for optimizing performance and ensuring safety, yet conventional methods are often impractical for real-time applications. This study proposes a novel deep learning framework capable of simultaneously predicting all three parameters using data from a single, short-term current pulse. Three advanced model architectures are designed and compared: a long short-term memory (LSTM) sequence-to-sequence model, an Attention-LSTM variant, and a multi-task learning (MTL) Transformer. The models are trained and validated on a comprehensive dataset from eight batteries under various temperatures, aging levels, and SOCs. Results demonstrate the MTL Transformer achieves superior overall performance, yielding the lowest test mean squared errors for SOC (0.1172%) and SOH (0.2221%). Concurrently, the Attention-LSTM model excels at high-fidelity EIS prediction with a minimal test error of 0.043 mΩ. With inference times under 17 ms, this work presents a hardware-agnostic, data-driven solution that enables comprehensive and real-time battery diagnostics, marking a significant advancement in battery management systems.

records.abstract: The surging structural failure of the Short- and Medium-Span (SMS) bridges underscores the need for structural safety monitoring and assessment. However, it is impossible to install the Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) systems comprehensively on all SMS bridges in the traffic networks due to budget limitations. To address this limitation, a lightweight SHM framework for the SMS bridge network is proposed based on a physics-encoded unsupervised deep learning architecture, where merely a single sensor is installed on each bridge. It integrates physics-based and data-driven modules to learn the nonlinear mapping relationships between the structural responses across different bridges. In the physics-based modules, the vehicle-induced quasi-static responses are extracted by using a Butterworth filter, and subsequently, they are used to identify the vehicular spatiotemporal information to construct the physics-informed temporal masks. In the data-driven modules, the physics-informed masks and geometric constraints are encoded into a multi-branch deep convolutional autoencoder. The measured responses of a source bridge are mapped to those of the target adjacent bridges, where the response reconstruction error is formulated as the loss function. Subsequently, the probability density pruning technique is adopted to collect the damage-sensitive indices from the loss values among different bridge pairs. These cross-bridge damage indices in a bridge network are integrated to identify the individual abnormal bridge. Numerical and laboratory experiments on simply supported beam bridges have been conducted under multi-vehicle dynamic loading, diverse sensor configurations, and multiple damage conditions. The damage index sensitivity is 151.3% with 10% stiffness reduction in 1/10 length of the beam.

records.abstract: Most machine learning models for predicting flowing bottomhole pressure (FBHP) are either black-box models, which offer high accuracy but lack interpretability, and white-box models, which provide transparency but often lack the flexibility or predictive power needed to capture nuances in the data. They are also predominantly data-driven, often ignoring physical laws, which can lead to accurate but physically inconsistent predictions. To bridge this gap, a physics-guided transformer model is proposed for FBHP in inclined production wells, addressing the trade-off between accuracy and interpretability. The model employs a dual-input architecture combining physical variables with sequential production data and enforces physical consistency via domain-informed loss functions. Trained and tested on 1329 samples from four production wells, the model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 38.31 psia (pounds per square inch absolute), root mean square error (RMSE) of 77.19 psia, and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 1.10%. To achieve interpretability, symbolic regression was used to derive a closed-form expression that captures physical trends which was validated via sensitivity analysis, yielding an MAE of 158.03 psia, RMSE of 233.37 psia, and MAPE of 3.83%. Uncertainty quantification was implemented using Monte Carlo Dropout, producing an average lower bound to upper bound (P10–P90) prediction spread of approximately 135 psia and a well-calibrated 95% prediction interval (miscalibration score = 0.030). Trend analysis showed that both the physics-guided transformer model and the symbolic regression equation captured trends consistent with physics. The framework delivers a high-performance, interpretable model that maintains physical plausibility in FBHP prediction.

records.abstract: Log anomaly detection is essential for system monitoring in cloud computing and microservice architectures. Current methodologies face substantial challenges including ambiguity in template extraction, domain-specific vocabulary difficulties, and outlier influence on feature selection. These issues impede practical implementation in resource-constrained environments requiring real-time detection, creating a technological gap that diminishes system reliability. This paper presents Optimized Principal Component Analysis (OPCA), a lightweight framework enabling efficient real-time anomaly detection through three innovations. First, an enhanced Drain-based log parsing module incorporates heuristic token splitting and optimized similarity calculations to improve template extraction accuracy while preserving semantic information. Second, Log-Specific Word Embedding (LSWE) integrates contrastive vocabularies with domain-specific semantic enhancement via offline pre-training and online out-of-vocabulary management, effectively capturing log semantics. Finally, a robust Principal Component Analysis (PCA) framework employs adaptive loss functions to mitigate outlier influence on principal component detection, enabling anomaly detection with minimal online training requirements, as the principal component estimation requires only a small set of normal log samples once the LSWE embeddings have been pre-trained offline. Experimental results demonstrate OPCA's strong performance, achieving F1-scores of 0.995 on Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) and 0.984 on BlueGene/L (BGL), while processing logs at 4750 samples per second on HDFS, up to 357-fold faster than graph-based methods, with F1-scores within 0.2 to 1.3 percentage points of the best-performing baseline on each dataset.

records.abstract: Current assessments of crop light in agrivoltaic systems typically depend on the average amount of photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) over a certain period. However, this method does not provide adequate details on how light varies with shadows, which is important for crop productivity. The artificial intelligence (AI) component of this research will utilize an explainable AI framework that combines analytical methods for determining solar geometry, a solar energy simulation every hour using PVsyst software, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based attribution of features, and a new metric called the Light Stability Index (LSI), which will allow us to quantify the amount of variability in temporal PAR without regard to the amount of irradiance received at that time. The application to engineering involves the study and optimal design of a vertical east-west bifacial agrivoltaic system with an electrical capacity of 1.224 MW-peak in Badarganj, Bangladesh. In this study, SHAP analysis found that shadow persistence time and solar elevation angle are two key factors responsible for LSI performance, contributing a combined 60–70 percent to the variance, and also showing nonlinear saturation behavior beyond the critical value of shadow persistence time. Sensitivity analysis showed that the LSI did not vary across scales or irradiance ranges. From this study, it can be concluded that light stability at the crop level is determined by shadow geometry and not irradiance.

records.abstract: The wax sand nanoparticle in water advances thermal transport where controlled heat transfer is critical. The inclusion of wax enables latent heat storage, while sand nanoparticles stabilize temperature gradients. This combination improves heat transport rates under varying operating conditions. This research examines the effects of E-shaped geometry and wax–sand nanoparticle in water on transport manifestations using an physics-informed neural network structure. The governing nanofluidics model is established with nonlinear partial differential equations. Limited-memory Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno algorithm is employed to ensure precise and steady convergence. The results exhibit that the E-shaped geometry upgrades spatial limitation and thermal performance, while the addition of wax and sand nanoparticles improves heat transfer properties. This neural scheme captures complicated physical behavior without demanding large datasets. The given framework indicates a reliable and dependable tool for analysis of ambiguous exchange phenomena in geometries relevant to cutting edge energy systems.

records.abstract: Automatic generation of chest radiology reports is pivotal for clinical decision-making, as it reduces radiologists’ diagnostic workload and mitigates the risk of missed findings. However, effective cross-modal semantic alignment remains challenging due to two key issues: (1) the inherent heterogeneity in feature representations between image and text modalities, and (2) the lack of semantic awareness in conventional negative sample selection strategies. The former introduces redundant and interfering signals that degrade alignment quality, while the latter misclassifies semantically similar samples as negatives, blurring decision boundaries and weakening discriminative power. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework, Cross-modal Orthogonal Adaptive Contrastive Learning (COACL), which enhances image–text semantic alignment and improves chest report generation through three core components: (1) a Modal Orthogonalization Module (MOM) that applies Schmidt orthogonalization to decouple image and text features into orthogonal subspaces. (2) a Gated Fusion Module (GFM) with dual-stream gated architecture to dynamically highlight salient semantic regions and enhance modality complementarity. (3) an Adaptive Contrastive Learning Module (ACLM) that employs a triplet comparison mechanism to adjust negative sample hardness based on semantic similarity and feature uniformity, progressively sharpening decision boundaries. Experiments on the benchmark IU-Xray and MIMIC-CXR datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across multiple metrics, and ablation studies substantiate the necessity of each module.

records.abstract: Smart agriculture requires robust, real-time, and highly accurate plant disease identification systems capable of performing reliably across diverse environmental conditions. This paper presents a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates the You Only Look Once version 5 object detection model with a Convolutional Neural Network classification head for precise plant disease identification. The proposed pipeline begins with data acquisition using the Plant Diseases Classification benchmark dataset, followed by advanced preprocessing through the Perona-Malik Anisotropic Diffusion algorithm for noise suppression and Elastic Distortion for data augmentation. Disease-affected regions are then precisely isolated using Watershed-based gradient segmentation, after which Speeded-Up Robust Features extraction guided by Hessian-matrix keypoint detection is applied. The pipeline concludes with end-to-end classification using the proposed hybrid deep learning framework across four crop health categories: Healthy, Rust, Powdery Mildew, and Slug damage. Rigorous experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed model consistently achieves 98.97% accuracy, 98.86% precision, 98.88% recall, and 98.87% F1-score, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines, including EfficientNetwork, standalone You Only Look Once version 5, Vision Transformers, and standard convolutional neural network architectures, by margins of up to 5.97 percentage points over comparable deep learning baselines. Near-perfect agreement between model predictions and ground-truth labels is further supported by a Cohen's Kappa coefficient of 0.9843. The system's two-stage localisation architecture delivers a computationally efficient and scalable solution well-suited for edge deployment within Internet of Things-enabled precision agriculture systems. This work contributes a reproducible, mathematically grounded methodology alongside a comprehensive ablation study, establishing the proposed hybrid deep learning framework as a strong benchmark for automated crop health monitoring.

records.abstract: The growing penetration of renewables and flexible demand-side resources makes microgrid economic dispatch heavily dependent on accurate forecasting, uncertainty modeling, and reliable demand response (DR) execution. However, practical DR actions often suffer from demand response delays (DRD) after dispatch signals, causing deviations between scheduled and actual load adjustments. To address this issue, this paper proposes a DRD-aware economic dispatch framework for microgrids by integrating time-series forecasting, generative scenario construction, and robust two-stage optimization. In the forecasting stage, a transfer learning-based Informer (TL-Informer) model is developed, in which a three-stage fine-tuning strategy is adopted to improve short-term load prediction accuracy under limited-data conditions. To characterize forecasting uncertainty, a two-stage linear variational diffusion generation framework (LV-DGF) is further proposed. In the first stage, a linear transformer-based variational autoencoder (LTVAE) is designed to achieve efficient long-sequence modeling and heterogeneous feature embedding. In the second stage, a score-based diffusion model is introduced to perform latent-space sampling and reconstruction, thereby enhancing both the physical consistency and statistical diversity of generated scenarios. Based on the predicted load and generated uncertainty scenarios, a DRD-aware robust two-stage optimization model is established to quantify the impact of delayed DR on operating costs and scheduling performance. Case studies demonstrate that DRD significantly affects microgrid dispatch decisions, and that neglecting such delays may lead to underestimated operating costs and reduced scheduling reliability. The results confirm the practical applicability of the proposed framework in supporting delay-aware microgrid scheduling and cost evaluation.

records.abstract: Accurate brain tumour analysis from magnetic resonance imaging requires both image-level classification and pixel-level segmentation. However, many deep learning approaches either handle these tasks separately or combine them in tightly coupled frameworks that may cause interference between tumour localisation and diagnostic prediction. This study proposes the Attention Long Short-Term Memory Segmentation Boundary Network (ALSB-Net), a lightweight stage-wise artificial intelligence framework for joint brain tumour segmentation and binary tumour/no-tumour classification. The artificial intelligence (AI) contribution is a stage-wise architecture that first learns tumour regions and boundary information using a constructed transfer-learning encoder incorporating selected transferred convolutional feature-extraction layers, bidirectional long short-term memory contextual modelling, attention refinement, and boundary-aware supervision, and then performs classification using detached feature representations to reduce task interference. The engineering application is demonstrated through integration into a Picture Archiving and Communication System-oriented research prototype for image viewing, reporting, and similar-case review. The framework was evaluated using an image/slice-level dataset combining public lower-grade glioma magnetic resonance imaging data with anonymised clinical scans collected from Iraqi hospitals. The classification dataset contained 5020 images, and the segmentation subset contained 3933 image-mask pairs. ALSB-Net achieved 95.4% classification accuracy, a 94.3% F1-score, and a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve of 0.988. For segmentation, it achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.9250, an intersection over union of 0.8120, and a 95th percentile Hausdorff distance of 2.85 mm. With 8.5233 million parameters, the framework provides efficient AI-assisted brain tumour analysis, while broader multi-centre validation remains necessary before routine clinical deployment.

records.abstract: Resin-based Liquid Chromatography (LC) is crucial for pharmaceutical manufacturing, but optimizing its process by conventional Design of Experiment is resource intensive. Numerical modelling techniques like Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) offer virtual platform to analyse flow and solute concentration distribution within LC column. Present study develops an opensource CFD solver under non-binding condition, benchmarking it against two experimental cases under different flow rates (Reynolds number in range of 0.02 to 0.096). The simulation results are in very good agreement with experimental ones (average coefficient of determination (R^{2}) score of 0.990 ± 0.003 for experimental case 1 and 0.969 ± 0.039 for experimental case 2). Further, an advanced meshless approach, Physics Informed Neural Network (PINN) is explored as a potential solver for the application of LC. A simplified 1-dimensional governing equation under non-binding is used for PINN based solver, and the predicted results are tested against experiment and CFD simulated results. For the studied range, PINN predicted results are in very good agreement with the experimental ones (average R^{2} of 0.990 ± 0.005 for experimental case 1 and 0.963 ± 0.047 for experimental case 2) and also replicated the CFD simulated ones with the advantage of reduced computational time (an average of 2.5 min for PINN versus 28 h of CFD simulations). However, the PINN predictions deviated from CFD result under high flow rate and strong dispersions (superficial condition for protein separation). For the studied LC conditions, the developed PINN based solver showed a promising alternative of conventional numerical modelling techniques.

records.abstract: Mismatch removal is a critical post-processing step for improving the reliability of remote sensing optical image matching. Existing methods generally rely on local-consensus verification, global geometric estimation, or dense graph-based reasoning. However, local approaches have limited receptive fields, global models are often inadequate for complex non-rigid or nonlinear distortions, and dense graphs may cause high computational cost and noisy message propagation. To address these issues, we propose a supervised graph learning framework that formulates mismatch removal as a graph neural network-based node classification task. Each putative correspondence is treated as a graph node, and motion-aware local preservation features are encoded using Kendall rank correlation and the longest common subsequence, providing discriminative cues for outlier rejection. To enhance efficiency and robustness, vector-field-consistency-based edge pruning is introduced to construct a sparse graph, suppressing unreliable message passing while reducing computational overhead. Built upon graph sample-and-aggregate network, the proposed network propagates neighborhood information through sparse global connections, effectively integrating local feature distinctiveness with global spatial coherence. Experiments on in-domain and cross-domain datasets show that our method achieves comparable or superior performance to representative state-of-the-art local-consensus, optimization-based, and learning-based methods. In cross-dataset mismatch-removal evaluation, the proposed method improves the F-score by up to 2.74 percentage points over the strongest competing verification baseline.

records.abstract: This study addresses multi-robot collaborative anomaly handling challenges in self-driving scientific laboratories, where anomalies cause distorted results, equipment damage and safety risks. For Artificial Intelligence (AI) contributions, we design a hierarchical large language model (LLM)-driven intelligent task planning framework for dynamic action decomposition and adjustment, and propose an anomaly-triggered cross-behavior tree expansion algorithm with a spatiotemporal propagation suppression strategy to realize real-time anomaly localization and management. For engineering applications, we build a high-fidelity simulation engine for silicone preparation and a physical multi-robot experimental system, designing three representative anomaly tasks (spatial, temporal, hybrid) for validation. Experimental results show that at 50% anomaly probability, the framework achieves a 78.67% task success rate (74.45% higher than the baseline) and shortens the task duration by 150 s (1476.67\to 1326.67 s). Both simulated and real-world tests verify that the proposed AI methods effectively enhance the system’s fault tolerance and flexibility. This work provides a novel AI-driven engineering solution for the full automation transformation of scientific laboratories.

records.abstract: Global sensitivity analysis (GSA) of nonlinear seismic responses is essential for identifying the dominant uncertain parameters governing structural performance, yet its practical application remains computationally demanding because it requires repeated nonlinear time–history analyses over uncertain parameter spaces. This challenge becomes even more severe in partial structural updating problems, where conventional surrogate models are typically reconstructed from scratch for each updated configuration, resulting in poor sample efficiency and limited reuse of previously acquired information. To address this issue, this study proposes an adaptive-sampling meta-learning Gaussian process framework for global sensitivity analysis (ASMLGP–GSA). The proposed framework transfers prior knowledge from structurally related meta-tasks to initialize the surrogate model of new target tasks, and then progressively refines the target-task surrogate through a cross-validation–Voronoi-based adaptive sampling strategy. A subdomain-importance stopping criterion is further introduced to terminate enrichment in a practical and computationally efficient manner. The framework is validated using three benchmark examples: a nonlinear two-degree-of-freedom Bouc–Wen system, a two-story steel moment-resisting frame equipped with self-centering viscous dampers, and a realistic three-dimensional offshore wind turbine jacket structure. The results show that the proposed method achieves high predictive accuracy while reducing the number of additional high-fidelity simulations required for convergence by approximately 80%–90% relative to single-task baseline methods. The surrogate-based Sobol’ indices also agree well with direct Monte Carlo estimates and correctly identify the dominant uncertain parameters in both case studies. These results demonstrate that ASMLGP–GSA provides an accurate and sample-efficient computational framework for seismic uncertainty propagation and sensitivity analysis of partially updated nonlinear structural systems.

records.abstract: Steel Fiber-Reinforced Recycled Aggregate Concrete (SFR-RAC) represents a sustainable alternative to conventional concrete, yet its mechanical properties exhibit high variability due to the coupled effects of recycled aggregate variability, steel fiber characteristics, and mixture proportions. This study develops a machine learning based reverse design framework to accurately predict key mechanical properties (i.e., compressive strength and splitting tensile strength) and optimize mixture proportions for SFR-RAC. Using a comprehensive dataset comprising 465 compressive strength samples and 339 splitting tensile strength samples, four machine learning algorithms (i.e., Extreme Gradient Boosting (i.e., XGBoost), Random Forest (i.e., RF), Decision Tree (i.e., DT), and K-Nearest Neighbors (i.e., KNN)) were trained and hyperparameter-optimized via Bayesian optimization with 5-fold cross-validation. In the case of the ensemble models (i.e., RF and XGBoost), both models exhibited better predictive capabilities. The RF model obtained test-set coefficient of determination values of 0.897 for the compressive strength parameter and 0.866 for the splitting tensile strength parameter, respectively, using Bayesian optimization. On the other hand, the XGBoost model obtained test-set coefficient of determination values of 0.893 for the compressive strength parameter and 0.896 for the splitting tensile strength parameter. Model interpretability was enhanced through Shapley Additive Explanations analysis, identifying water-to-binder ratio and steel fiber volume fraction as the most influential features for compressive strength and splitting tensile strength, respectively. Multi-objective optimization using Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II successfully generated Pareto-optimal solutions, balancing compressive strength and cost under practical constraints. This inverse design approach further provided actionable mixture proportions tailored to target performance criteria.

Wind power time series are characterized by strong randomness, volatility, and non-stationarity, which poses severe challenges to accurate wind power forecasting and the stable operation of power grids. From an artificial intelligence (AI) perspective, this paper proposes a hybrid ultra-short-term wind power forecasting framework with three key methodological innovations: A data-driven adaptive component clustering strategy based on sample entropy and silhouette coefficient to objectively group wind power components; a Complexity-Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) Integrated Index (CSI) to guide secondary decomposition by combining structural complexity and signal quality; and a component-wise forecasting strategy with tailored deep learning models, including Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit with Attention (BiGRU-Attention), and Temporal Convolutional Network-Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit with Attention (TCN-BiGRU-Attention). From an engineering application perspective, the proposed method is validated on real-world wind power datasets from Wallonia, Belgium. records.abstract: Disc cutters are critical components of tunnel boring machines (TBM), yet existing wear monitoring methods are often restricted by harsh operating environments and still suffer from algorithmic limitations such as weak physical interpretability, insufficient generalization under varying operating parameters, and limited robustness when relying on single-source signals. This study proposes a novel intelligent disc cutter equipped with integrated temperature and vibration sensors. By establishing a dynamic model of the disc cutter, an Engineering-Optimized Physics-Data Neural Network (EOPD-NN) is utilized to reconstruct actual cutter ring loads. Furthermore, a decision-level information fusion framework—incorporating vibration, load, and temperature signals—is developed to predict the cutter wear state. The proposed monitoring algorithm relies only on localized cutter data. Experimental validation on a full-scale rotary cutting platform demonstrates that 94.29% of the sequence samples reconstructed by the EOPD-NN achieve a coefficient of determination (R^{2}) greater than 0.95 under different parameter conditions. Moreover, the proposed fusion strategy achieves a wear state recognition accuracy of about 96.5%. It also demonstrates exceptional interpretability within the domain. Ultimately, this intelligent disc cutter system offers a practical and reliable solution for cutter wear monitoring.

records.abstract: In this paper, enhance the computational models of human decision-making by proposing a novel sharded reinforcement learning framework based on the principle of machine unlearning. The work proposes a data sharding and selective machine unlearning approach to unlearn faulty behavior patterns. It overcomes the drawbacks of conventional reinforcement learning methods, in which the players tend to play the same deck over and over again, showing a lack of adaptability. These problems are frequently seen in tasks such as the Iowa gambling task. To handle this issue, the concept of machine unlearning is used. The proposed method detects repeated patterns of faulty behavior, such as repeated deck selections. Such patterns are corrected locally at the level of shards, while retaining the last stable expectancy state from the previous learning stage. The mean squared deviation was used to evaluate the model's performance. The results indicate that the unlearned model learns faster and has better performance in the early phases of learning. The framework supports behavioral adaptability by selectively excluding identified faulty shards while preserving previous valid learning. These findings show the potential of shard-based learning and selective unlearning in sequential decision-making.

records.abstract: Accurate brain tumour segmentation from Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) remains a major clinical challenge due to tumour heterogeneity, irregular morphology, blurred boundaries, low-contrast regions, and very small lesions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel lightweight deep learning framework for simultaneous brain tumour segmentation and classification based on the You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) segmentation architecture. The framework incorporates a pathology-aware lightweight backbone, a scale-reallocated segmentation hierarchy, and an additional extra-small segmentation head to improve the detection of small and irregular tumours. A multi-scale feature fusion strategy enhances segmentation accuracy while reducing model parameters by 80.5% and computational complexity by 57% compared with the baseline model. In addition, a novel adaptive training strategy, termed Best Adaptation Strategy (BAS), improves convergence stability, optimisation robustness, and model generalisation during training. Extensive experiments were conducted using a brain tumour segmentation dataset containing 801 magnetic resonance imaging scans, and the Figshare Brain Tumour (FBT) dataset containing 3064 multi-class tumour scans. The proposed framework achieved mean Average Precision (mAP) values of 97.7% and 99.4% at an Intersection over Union (IoU) threshold of 0.50, and 83.1% and 83.3% across thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95, respectively. These results outperform recent standard deep learning segmentation models, classical machine learning approaches, and other state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, deployment on a robotic platform demonstrates the practical feasibility and translational potential of the proposed framework for real-time diagnosis in limited-resource environments and artificial intelligence applications in healthcare.
