records.abstract: Elucidating chemo-mechanical degradation mechanisms and optimizing the design of lithium-ion battery electrodes require a deep understanding of the coupled chemo-mechanical behavior within real heterogeneous microstructures. However, traditional microstructure-based finite element (FE) simulations are computationally prohibitive for resolving such complex three-dimensional (3D) multiphysics fields. In this study, an end-to-end deep learning scheme is developed to directly predict the 3D coupled chemo-mechanical full-field responses of electrode microstructures from geometric information, without requiring any additional prior physical information. The microstructural geometries are generated using a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based stochastic reconstruction algorithm trained on scanning electron microscope (SEM) images of real electrodes. The prediction model is built on a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) comprising a hybrid CNN–Transformer generator and a multi-scale discriminator. This architecture enables the simultaneous prediction of 3D stress and lithium concentration fields. The proposed framework demonstrates high predictive accuracy, achieving average relative errors of approximately 4.4% for stress fields and 1.5% for concentration fields. Experimental validation further supports the predicted heterogeneous lithium concentration distributions. By reducing inference time to only tens of seconds while maintaining accuracy comparable to high-fidelity simulations, this work provides an efficient alternative for rapid multiphysics analysis and microstructure design of battery materials.

records.abstract: Ensuring safe and reliable operation of modern railway systems increasingly relies on data-driven monitoring and intelligent fault detection solutions. In recent years, deep learning has emerged as an effective paradigm for anomaly detection in railway applications, driven by the growing availability of heterogeneous sensor data collected from rolling stock and infrastructure. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of deep learning-based anomaly detection approaches developed for railway systems. The surveyed methods are systematically analyzed and organized using a unified taxonomy that captures the location of anomaly occurrence, data representation and manifestation, sensing modality, and temporal characteristics. Existing approaches, spanning convolutional neural networks, recurrent and attention-based architectures, autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, and transformer-based models, are further structured into major learning paradigms, including classification-based, prediction-based, reconstruction-based, and hybrid strategies. Beyond algorithmic design, this survey discusses key data-centric challenges and reviews commonly adopted evaluation practices and performance metrics. Practical deployment aspects are also addressed, including edge–cloud architectures, computational constraints, and hardware-aware optimization strategies for embedded railway applications. Building on this analysis, the survey introduces a decision-oriented framework that links anomaly characteristics, data properties, and operational constraints to appropriate detection paradigms and deployment configurations. By jointly considering learning models, data characteristics, evaluation protocols, and deployment constraints, this work provides engineers and researchers with a structured and application-oriented reference for selecting and deploying deep learning solutions for railway anomaly detection, while highlighting open challenges and future research directions toward reliable and scalable intelligent monitoring systems.

records.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a formidable paradigm for solving partial differential equations governing physical systems. Even so, their efficacy has been largely confined to regular geometries limiting their real-world engineering application in solid mechanics where components possess the complex shapes and realistic boundary conditions. To bridge this critical gap, we introduce the Physics-Informed Kolmogorov–Arnold Graph Attention Network (PI-GKAT), a novel physics-informed graph neural network framework designed for high-fidelity solid mechanics simulations on arbitrary geometries. Our architecture integrates Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) into a Graph Neural Network (GNN) backbone. This structural enhancement unlocks superior function approximation, enabling the simulation of complex nonlinear mechanics on arbitrary geometries. Meanwhile, a Graph Attention (GAT) mechanism is integrated into the message-passing process, allowing the network to selectively weight and learn the most relevant local physical and structural information. This unified architecture supports a broad spectrum of constitutive models, including linear elasticity and hyper-elasticity, while accommodating realistic material parameters through physics-constrained loss functions. Extensive validation on multiple test cases with complex geometries demonstrates the superior generalization performance and higher predictive accuracy of the proposed PI-GKAT framework across different geometric shapes and material types. We also evaluated our framework on regular geometry and compared its performance with existing representative methods. PI-GKAT provides a robust and efficient tool for solving a new class of complex engineering problems.

records.abstract: Accurate prediction of ocean multivariable fields such as sea surface temperature, salinity, seawater flow rate and wind stress is crucial for understanding ocean–atmosphere interactions and climate prediction. However, the existing methods often have problems such as low accuracy, lack of physical consistency and poor long-term stability. To solve these problems, Multi-Physical Spatial–Temporal Adaptive Memory Network was proposed. This model utilizes the Multi-dimensional Feature Perception Module to adaptively extract features and calibrate important feature responses, constructs ocean physical dynamics constraints based on the Multi-Physics Ocean Cell, and models multi-dimensional long-term dependencies by introducing the Spatio-Temporal Adaptive Memory Unit. Experiments based on Hybrid Coordinate Ocean Model data show that our model outperforms 14 advanced and physics-guided benchmark models within a 7-day prediction period, performing well in the prediction of seawater velocity and wind stress direction. Even in the 28-day long-term prediction, it maintained excellent performance. It has good universality and stability, and can provide technical support for ship safety, fishery resource management and renewable energy development.

records.abstract: This study develops a physics-guided machine learning framework for predicting the carbonation kinetics of basic oxygen furnace slag (BOFS) across different particle size fractions. Specifically, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) integrated shrinking core model (SCM) (PINN–SCM) was proposed, embedding governing kinetic equations into the learning process to enable time-resolved prediction of CaO conversion, CO_{2} uptake, and pH evolution. The PINN-SCM framework improves predictive accuracy compared to conventional SCM by enforcing mechanistic constraints and enabling continuous representation of evolving reaction-diffusion regimes. More importantly, the proposed model successfully captures nonlinear carbonation trajectories, including intermediate regime transitions that static SCM fails to resolve. A hybrid SCM-machine learning approach was further developed using residual learning, which further reduced prediction errors, particularly for CO_{2} uptake and diffusion-dominated regimes. The prediction trends are supported by thermogravimetric (TG) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) analyses, as well as scanning electron microscopy (SEM) observations revealing dense carbonate shells in coarse particles and porous reaction products in finer fractions. The findings show that SCM-informed machine learning models can capture multi-regime, particle-size-dependent carbonation behaviour more effectively than static and mixed-control SCM fitting under the studied wet-carbonation conditions, while retaining mechanistic constraints and apparent kinetic interpretability.

records.abstract: Recently, Contrastive Language-Image Pre-Training (CLIP) has been widely used for zero-shot two-dimensional (2D) anomaly detection, while zero-shot three-dimensional (3D) anomaly detection still needs further research. Existing CLIP-based methods use the similarity between image features and prompt features for image–text detection, ignoring that image features can be used independently for anomaly detection. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Hybrid-modality zero-shot 3D Anomaly Detection method based on CLIP (HAD-CLIP). Specifically, in addition to image–text detection, HAD-CLIP introduces a detection head after the image encoder, which is used for image-only detection. Considering that the training samples and test samples come from different datasets, the normal prompt feature learned based on the training samples may not effectively represent the normality of the test samples. HAD-CLIP only learns the anomaly prompt feature, and this paper designs a clipped similarity loss for single prompt feature learning. Then, the image-only detection and image–text detection at different stages are jointly used as hybrid-modality zero-shot 3D anomaly detection. Experimental results on the MVTec 3D Anomaly Detection (MVTec 3D-AD) and Real 3D Anomaly Detection (Real3D-AD) datasets show that the proposed HAD-CLIP achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot 3D anomaly detection performance at both the object and point levels. The effectiveness of HAD-CLIP is further validated on a real-world vehicle stamped parts dataset.

records.abstract: Recent advances in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) are increasingly influencing medical imaging by enhancing diagnostic accuracy, key task automation, early disease detection, and personalized treatments. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) serves as the foundation of medical image analysis, showcasing improved results in classification, segmentation, and detection tasks. However, intrinsic limitations, including inability to accurately represent long-range dependencies, large data requirement for training, limited interpretability, and data privacy constraints have promoted interest in alternative artificial intelligence (AI) paradigms. Emerging approaches including vision transformers (ViTs), generative adversarial networks (GANs), explainable AI (XAI), and federated learning (FL) are reshaping the landscape of medical image generation, analysis, and deployment in clinical environments. ViTs have shown superior efficacy than CNNs in capturing global contextual information through self-attention mechanisms. GANs are offering innovative solutions for data augmentation, image enhancement, and modality translation. XAI techniques improve interpretability and trustworthiness of complex DL architectures applied on image data, thus supporting their safe and fair deployment in healthcare. FL enables collaborative model training across multiple decentralized medical centers while preserving data privacy. This study synthesizes insights from over 120 journal articles published between 2020 and 2025 and presents a unified conceptual framework integrating imaging modalities, emerging DL architectures, interpretability considerations, and privacy-aware deployment strategies. Additionally, it highlights key applications, benchmark datasets, existing challenges, and future research directions, offering practical guidance for researchers and clinicians in model selection and responsible AI implementation.

records.abstract: Protein phosphorylation is a key post-translational modification involved in signal transduction, disease progression and therapeutic regulation. Reliable phosphorylation-site prediction remains challenging because existing methods often have limited feature integration, weak generalization and reduced performance on low-sample residue types. Here, we propose AdaptIPs, a dual-channel deep-learning framework for phosphorylation-site prediction. AdaptIPs integrates residue-level sequence representations with pretrained ESMC embeddings through element-wise multiplicative fusion, and uses Bahdanau attention, mirror loss and adaptive early stopping to improve feature learning and training stability. To address the limited number of tyrosine phosphorylation sites, we further use transfer learning from serine/threonine site prediction to tyrosine-site prediction. On independent test sets, AdaptIPs achieved an accuracy of 84.48% and an AUC of 91.83% for serine/threonine sites, and an accuracy of 92.86% and an AUC of 94.33% for tyrosine sites. Comparative experiments, ablation analysis and fusion-strategy evaluation confirmed the contribution of the dual-channel architecture and multiplicative fusion. AdaptIPs provides a reproducible framework for phosphorylation-site prediction and may support broader few-shot biological sequence prediction tasks. The source code is available at https://github.com/scarlet211/AdaptIPs.

records.abstract: The drug discovery process is a deep multi-stage procedure in which generative artificial intelligence, specifically diffusion-based generative models, has been identified as having significant potential to address critical challenges in drug discovery, including de novo molecule design, structure-based ligand generation, and pharmacological property optimization. Unlike other popular generative models such as variational autoencoders (VAEs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs), diffusion models are found to possess more stable training behaviors and better ability to capture complex molecular distributions in both two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) chemical space. This review is a critical analysis of diffusion-based generative models in drug discovery. The analysis is based on a transparent literature search process. The literature search process includes articles published between 2017 and 2025 in peer-reviewed journals. The articles are obtained from Scopus, PubMed, and arXiv. In addition, we analyze the applications of diffusion models in different stages of drug discovery, such as molecule generation, protein-ligand docking, scaffold hopping, and conformation prediction. Moreover, we analyze the benchmarking of diffusion models on popular datasets such as Quantum Mechanics 9 (QM9), Geometric Ensemble of Molecules for drug discovery (GEOM-DRUG), CrossDocked2020 (a structure-based docking benchmark), Protein Data Bank binding data (PDBbind), and popular platforms such as Molecular Sets (MOSES) and GuacaMol. Unlike prior surveys, this review adopts an explicit literature selection protocol, provides per-model computational complexity analysis, and critically examines both benchmarking pitfalls and the emerging transition from denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) toward flow matching as a distinct generative paradigm. We demonstrate that existing metrics such as validity, novelty, and docking scores do not provide a complete understanding of chemical and biological relevance. In addition, we identify that synthetic feasibility constraints are not considered in existing studies, there is a lack of experimental validation, and evaluation protocols are not consistent. In addition, we discuss the existing limitations of explainable artificial intelligence in generative molecular modeling.

records.abstract: Electromagnetic field modeling is important for remote sensing and target detection, but accurate solutions remain challenging in the presence of heterogeneous interfaces, multiple material parameters, anisotropic media, and multidimensional field coupling. This paper proposes a Flux-Conserved Physics-Informed Neural Networks framework that combines domain decomposition with a discontinuous Galerkin-inspired residual formulation and numerical-flux-based interface coupling. Roe numerical flux is adopted as the specific upwind-type flux in the interface loss to promote physically consistent information transfer across subdomains. Hard boundary constraints, joint input–output normalization, gradient-normalization-based adaptive loss balancing, and a two-stage adaptive moment estimation and limited-memory Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno optimization strategy are also incorporated to improve training stability and accuracy. The framework is evaluated on four fixed benchmarks: a one-dimensional two-parameter time-domain layered model, a one-dimensional frequency-domain anisotropic model, a three-dimensional time-domain model, and a three-dimensional frequency-domain anisotropic model. Across the tested configurations, the predictions agree well with discontinuous Galerkin and finite-element reference solutions, with maximum relative field errors below five percent and approximately fifty percent fewer residual sub-elements than the reference discretizations used for comparison. In the tested one-dimensional benchmark, the framework required approximately 500 s of offline training but became computationally advantageous after approximately 536 repeated evaluations. Comparisons with conventional, conservative, and extended physics-informed neural networks indicate improved interface consistency and convergence stability. These results support the effectiveness of the proposed framework for forward electromagnetic field prediction under the examined configurations. Generalization to unseen parameters, frequencies, and geometries, and extension to parametric and inverse modeling, are left for future study.

records.abstract: Real-time thermal management of high-power microchannel cooling systems requires fast and accurate reconstruction of temperature, pressure, and velocity fields. However, full three-dimensional (3D) computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations remain computationally prohibitive for online deployment, while purely data-driven surrogate models may violate governing thermal-fluid constraints. This study develops an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled physics-informed surrogate framework, the Dynamic Weighted Learning Rate Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts Physics-Informed Neural Network (DWLR-MMoE-PINN), for real-time field reconstruction in microchannel cooling. The proposed framework integrates three problem-specific components into a unified workflow: a corrected reduced-order model for efficient dataset generation, learned soft expert routing to mitigate multiphysics task interference, and component-wise dynamic loss normalization to balance heterogeneous physical objectives. The corrected two-dimensional (2D) model decreased the composite error by 37.4% compared with the uncorrected counterpart. Under a unified case-level learning protocol, DWLR-MMoE-PINN reduced the final validation loss by 31.0% and the overall out-of-distribution error by 49.5% relative to DWLR-PINN. The trained surrogate enables microsecond-level point-wise prediction and reconstructs the exported spatial field of one case in 0.116 s, giving speedups of more than three orders of magnitude over the corrected 2D solver and four orders of magnitude over the full 3D simulation. These results support DWLR-MMoE-PINN as a real-time field-reconstruction surrogate for future digital-twin applications, while sensor integration, online calibration, and closed-loop thermal control remain future work.

records.abstract: In Internet of Things (IoT) systems, blockchain and Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques have a major trend due to their significant. However, security, efficiency, and scalability are challenged due to the integration of AI techniques, which generate redundant data. To overcome these challenges, a novel Efficient Channel Attention-assisted Dense Transformer (ECA-deTrans) based data anomaly detection with blockchain is proposed for forensic evidence integrity verification. Initially, the raw data is collected from the repository and pre-processed. Feature extraction is performed using feature extraction using a Hybrid Autoencoder with 1 Dimensional Convolutional Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (HAE-1DBiLSTM). Based on the extracted features, ECA-deTrans performs forensic anomaly detection. Then, the smart contract system performs blockchain based integrity verification using Keccak-based Secure Hash Algorithm-3 with Enhanced Logistic Map (SHA-3-ELMC) chaotic algorithm. The blockchain creates an immutable audit trail that guarantees accountability, transparency, and compliance by permanently storing all AI discoveries, smart contract operations, and verification outcomes. Based on the simulation, the accuracy of 99.74%, precision of 99.48%, recall of 99.63%, F1-score of 99.55%, Mean Average Error (MAE) of 0.58%, throughput of 28.251 transactions per second (tps), and latency of 0.395 s were achieved. The experimental results demonstrate the significant of the proposed approach for real-time applicability.

records.abstract: The dynamic modulus, a critical parameter for asphalt mixture viscoelasticity and pivotal for pavement engineering, conventionally faces determination challenges due to high costs, extensive data dependency, and limited physical insight. To overcome these, this study introduces a dual-driven predictive framework that integrates physical knowledge with data science principles. Initially, Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) was employed to quantify the influence weights of twelve material composition parameters. Subsequently, leveraging K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), and Random Forest (RF) algorithms, a sensitive feature space was meticulously constructed. Critically, established positive correlations between softening point, asphalt type, and dynamic modulus were encoded as physics-based constraints within a Backpropagation Neural Network (BP-NN), culminating in a physics-informed, data-driven dynamic modulus prediction model. Rigorous multi-error index cross-validation and stability evaluation confirmed model robustness. Results revealed void volume and asphalt aggregate ratio as dominant dynamic modulus influencers, while apparent density of mineral powder and asphalt specific gravity could diminish generalization. Compared to data-driven counterparts, the proposed physical-data-driven model exhibited a marginal increase in Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 41–46 Megapascals (MPa) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 28–29 MPa, yet consistently maintained Coefficient of Determination (R^{2}) > 0.96 and a significantly narrowed prediction confidence interval. These findings underscore that embedding physical constraints substantially enhances model stability and rationality, ensuring adherence to engineering principles while largely preserving high accuracy. This research offers a robust methodology for accurate dynamic modulus prediction and optimized material design in asphalt mixtures, advancing scientific road design and sustainable pavement engineering.

records.abstract: In industrial fluid engineering, continuous monitoring of unsteady flows is essential for mechanism analysis and process optimization, but is often limited by the hardware cost and data-storage burden of high-frequency particle image velocimetry systems. This study considers an artificial intelligence application in which sparse and short-duration particle image velocimetry observations are used to reconstruct flow-field evolution and to extrapolate the flow over a short future window. We propose a Mamba-integrated physics-informed neural network framework for this task. The implemented artificial intelligence uses a Mamba selective state-space sequence model to learn temporal advancement from probe-wise velocity histories, while a physics-informed neural network reconstructs continuous velocity and pressure fields under incompressible Navier–Stokes residual constraints. A mutual learning procedure links these two parts: the physics-informed reconstruction supplies residual-filtered temporal samples for sequence learning, and the learned temporal prior then guides reconstruction in the interval without observations. Evaluated on standard two-dimensional laminar cylinder-flow benchmarks and demonstrated qualitatively on real experimental particle image velocimetry data, the proposed framework reduces extrapolation root mean square error by up to approximately 61% compared with a standard physics-informed neural network baseline and maintains a reported three-cylinder extrapolation coefficient of determination of 0.986596 over the reported extrapolation window from 5 to 7 s. These results indicate that the proposed framework can serve as an artificial intelligence post-processing method for sparse-flow diagnostics, although broader deployment still requires validation under more complex flow and measurement conditions.

records.abstract: Precise traffic flow forecasting continues to be difficult because of the intricate spatio-temporal interdependencies within transportation networks. While existing methods have achieved no-table progress, two critical limitations persist: (i) insufficient synergistic integration of spatio- temporal features that reflect real traffic dynamics, and (ii) ineffective capture of multi-timescale traffic node features. To resolve these concerns, we propose an Asymmetric Spatio-Temporal Synergistic Graph Neural Network (ASGNN). Our model introduces three key innovations: First, a learnable synergistic spatio-temporal adjacency matrix that dynamically unifies temporal and spatial relationships within the same latent dimension. Second, an asymmetric feature extraction mechanism that adaptively applies enhanced synergistic modeling to pivotal nodes. Third, a hierarchical architecture that progressively fuses multi-timescale node features into comprehensive global representations. To verify the effectiveness of our model in traffic flow forecasting, we conducted experiments on real-world datasets (PeMSD4 and PeMSD8), with detailed ablation studies confirming the contribution of each component.

records.abstract: Protein informatics increasingly requires artificial intelligence models for analyzing biological sequences, structures, interactions, and drug-related targets. Transformer architectures, built on self-attention mechanisms, have become widely used in this field, but their reliability remains dependent on data coverage, biological context, and evaluation protocol. This survey critically reviews over 100 representative studies on Transformer-based methods for protein research. We organize the literature through a two-level taxonomy that separates model-class principles from problem-space applications, covering sequence-only language modeling, geometry-aware prediction, multimodal alignment, and generative design, together with structure prediction, function annotation, interaction analysis, drug discovery, and drug-target identification. We examine how pre-trained protein language models, structure-aware Transformers, and multimodal variants incorporate sequences, evolutionary profiles, and three-dimensional coordinates to address protein-specific constraints. We further synthesize key methodological issues, including geometric inductive bias, physical plausibility, scalability, uncertainty calibration, dataset bias, reproducibility, and generative-model evaluation. Through comparative tables and cross-domain analysis, this survey connects protein Transformer architectures to automated protein engineering, high-throughput drug screening, proteome-scale annotation, and laboratory-in-the-loop design. It evaluates these systems not only by predictive accuracy, but also by computational cost, latency, calibration, reproducibility, physical validation, and experimental utility, and concludes with a prioritized roadmap for deployable protein artificial intelligence.

records.abstract: This study develops a physics-informed, multi-source adaptive learning framework for predicting tunnel settlement during drill-and-blast excavation. Blasting vibration data, geological conditions, and monitoring measurements are integrated to capture complex spatiotemporal interactions. A Spatial Exponential Decay Weighted interpolation with Local Residual Correction (SEDW-LRC) method is proposed to enhance vibration features. The framework combines Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with an attention mechanism to model temporal dependencies, while Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) is introduced for feature evaluation and adaptive model fusion based on prediction performance. A case study of the Xingye tunnel demonstrates that the enhanced vibration representation improves prediction accuracy by 7.2%. The proposed framework outperforms standalone models, achieving accuracy gains of 7.3% over XGBoost, 8.2% over LSTM-Attention, and 18.3% over LSTM. The results highlight the importance of integrating vibration response in data-driven prediction, providing support for intelligent blasting control and construction optimization.

records.abstract: Medical imaging classifiers are increasingly used to inform clinical decision-making. However, these systems often operate under implicit assumptions of unconstrained treatment capacity. In reality, healthcare providers face severe resource constraints, ranging from radiologist time to surgical availability, necessitating models that align classification decisions with actionable capacity. We propose a novel deep learning framework for multi-class medical image classification that integrates resource-aware constraint optimization directly into neural network training. This approach enables knowledge-intensive engineering of predictive models tailored for clinical decision support under real-world treatment or computational constraints. Our method is particularly suited to common clinical scenarios such as staging cancer progression, grading knee osteoarthritis, or classifying skin lesions, where disease stages imply different treatment pathways but not all can be addressed due to resource limitations. We evaluate our method on two distinct medical imaging tasks: knee osteoarthritis severity grading from X-ray images and skin lesion classification from dermatoscopic images. Across both datasets, our approach demonstrates improved performance and constraint compliance over traditional predict-then-optimize pipelines, particularly under tight resource constraints Our results highlight the framework’s generalizability across diverse medical imaging modalities and class imbalance scenarios, making it a compelling tool for engineering intelligent diagnostic systems in healthcare.

records.abstract: Ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) is one of the most promising cement-based materials for sustainable and resilient infrastructure, owing to its exceptional strength and durability. Nevertheless, the complex interactions among fiber bridging, aggregate interlock, dowel action, and size-dependent fracture mechanics in shear-critical UHPC beams are not adequately captured by current design codes, leading to large prediction scatter and uncertain safety margins. To address these limitations, this study introduces a physics-informed and interpretable machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) framework, termed the Monotone Additive Interaction Network (Phys-MAIN), for design-oriented shear capacity prediction and resistance factor calibration of UHPC beams across four reinforcement configurations. The architecture embeds four configuration-specific submodels within an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS), where each submodel enforces physically consistent input–output relationships through monotone functions and bivariate interaction surfaces. Distribution-free conformal prediction intervals calibrated on held-out residuals provide finite-sample coverage guarantees without distributional assumptions. Model uncertainty is further characterized through the American Concrete Institute (ACI) 318 load and resistance factor design (LRFD) reliability calibration at a target reliability index of ${\beta }_{T}=3.5$, with resistance factors calibrated across four reinforcement configurations and five shear-mechanism sub-populations. Phys-MAIN achieves a cross-validated ${R}^{2}$ of 0.933 with a zero percent physical monotonicity violation rate. Configuration-specific calibration reveals that reinforcement type strongly governs the required safety margin, with calibrated resistance factors (for the fiber-containing configurations) ranging from 0.485 for fiber-only beams to 0.625 for fiber-with-prestress beams. To facilitate practical adoption, the framework is deployed as a user-friendly interactive tool available at https://twakjira.github.io/Phys_MAIN/.

records.abstract: In a broader sense, condition monitoring solutions can be either data-driven or physics-based. The performance and robustness of data-driven models largely depend on the quantity of training data and the interpretability level of the machine learning (ML) model (e.g., black box, white box, grey box). These models often suffer from limited interpretability, as their predictions do not necessarily adhere to underlying physical laws. In contrast, physics-based models are influenced by modeling assumptions, system complexity, computational cost, and the level of domain expertise required. Recently, increasing attention has been given to combining both paradigms, generally referred to as Physics Augmented Machine Learning (PAML). In this hybrid approach, physical knowledge can be integrated into any module of the ML framework. In this study, PAML methods are classified into three categories according to how physical information is embedded: Physics-guided Neural Network (PGNN), Physics-informed Neural Network (PINN), and Physics-encoded Neural Network (PENN), and a detailed analysis of their algorithmic frameworks and structural characteristics is provided. Furthermore, a review of their applications in the context of rotating machinery, including dynamic modeling, fault diagnostics, and fault prognostics is presented. Finally, several current challenges and future directions are outlined to support the integration and further development of physical information and machine learning-based approaches.

records.abstract: The transition of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) from simulation to real-world deployment presents significant challenges due to the simulation-to-reality (sim-to-real) gap, particularly concerning simplified electromechanical dynamics and energy optimization. To address these discrepancies, this paper proposes a hierarchical framework integrating bottom-up physics modeling, neural system identification, and energy-aware control. In contrast to conventional kinematic models, the developed high-fidelity environment explicitly integrates actuator dynamics, including voltage saturation, Back-Electromotive Force (Back-EMF), and transient delays, ensuring that the learned policies respect realistic physical constraints. Central to this framework is a novel context-aware neural architecture designed to decouple flight states from latent hardware signatures. This module achieves a hardware classification accuracy exceeding 97% and robust power estimation with a nominal Normalized Root Mean Square Error (NRMSE) of approximately 1.5%, effectively functioning as a virtual sensor. Leveraging these learned dynamics, we introduce an Energy-Cost-Optimized Reinforcement Learning (Eco-RL) policy that couples a Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) planner with a robust Feedback Linearization and Model Reference Adaptive Control (FBL-MRAC) execution layer. By incorporating the learned power consumption into the reinforcement learning reward loop, the agent synthesizes momentum-conserving trajectories that strategically trade off altitude potential against air density variations. Extensive validation across five heterogeneous hardware classes demonstrates an overall energy reduction of 19.8% across randomized sorties, which consolidates into a highly significant 13.5% efficiency gain under strict pair-wise evaluations compared to standard policies, confirming the efficacy of physics-informed Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) in optimizing flight efficiency.

records.abstract: Feature extraction and classification are key tasks in brain-computer interfaces (BCI) based on motor imagery (MI) electroencephalography (EEG), which have applications in motor function compensation and rehabilitation. However, existing deep learning methods suffer from issues such as insufficient utilization of neurophysiological priors (event-related desynchronization/synchronization) and inadequate handling of multi-domain (spectral, spatial, temporal) information. To address these problems, this study proposes a parallel hybrid network integrating traditional feature engineering and deep learning, which differs from serial cascade and purely data-driven paradigms: it integrates one-versus-rest filter bank common spatial patterns (for extracting spatial-spectral features), residual convolutional neural network (for learning nonlinear spatio-temporal features), dynamic graph convolutional network (for analyzing feature relations), and gated recurrent unit (for capturing long-term temporal patterns). Additionally, we use an attention mechanism to dynamically fuse features and a composite loss function to enhance feature clustering performance. Our method was validated on three public datasets: BCI Competition IV-2a (4-class, 85.28 ± 10.43%), IV-2b (2-class, 89.75 ± 8.02%), and the dataset by Kaya et al., 2018, Sci Data (3-class, 78.66 ± 8.31%; 5-class, 59.80 ± 8.69%; 6-class, 65.33 ± 8.04%). Results show that our method significantly outperforms recent methods and traditional methods, with a reduction in accuracy fluctuation. Ablation experiments show the contribution of each module, with accuracy drops of 1.5%-2.5% after removing any single component. This study demonstrates that the hybrid network model, by complementing traditional feature engineering and deep learning, breaks through the limitations of a single technical route and provides an approach with accuracy and robustness for multi-class MI-EEG decoding.

records.abstract: Pile caps in bridge foundations serve as critical load-bearing components, directly influencing structural safety and economic efficiency. However, the current reinforcement design of double-pile caps still relies on engineering experience and manual verification, resulting in low efficiency. To address this limitation, this study proposes a physics-informed multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) method, termed Rein-MARL, for intelligent reinforcement design. Rein-MARL integrates a physics-guided reinforcement learning environment with a knowledge-informed reward function. By decomposing the collaborative design process of rebars into multiple sub-tasks, a multi-agent system (MAS) is employed to independently design different components. Validation using practical design cases demonstrates that the artificial intelligence (AI)-generated reinforcement schemes satisfy both code-based safety and economic requirements. Compared with engineer-designed layouts, Rein-MARL achieves average relative errors of 9.8% in load-bearing capacity and 3.6% in steel consumption. Remarkably, Rein-MARL reduces the design time to only 0.5% of that required by the manual process, indicating a substantial improvement in reinforcement automation and providing a theoretical basis for future intelligent design in bridge systems.

records.abstract: Image classification is a fundamental task in computer vision, requiring methods that balance high accuracy with computational efficiency. In this study, we introduce an efficient image classification approach that combines feature extraction using Vision Transformer (ViT) with an improved probabilistic classification technique, referred to as Enhanced Bayes. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, three experiments were conducted. The first experiment assessed overall classification performance, while the second and third experiments compared our approach with ten models, including both traditional machine learning and deep learning models. The results demonstrate that our method performed better than ten existing classification models, including Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Residual Network with 50 layers (ResNet50), Visual Geometry Group with 16 layers (VGG16), GoogLeNet Inception version 3 (Inception V3), Inception Residual Network version 2 (Inception ResNet-V2), and the original ViT, achieves higher classification accuracy while maintaining low computational cost. Additionally, we conducted a comparative analysis of different feature extraction methods. The combination of ViT-based features with the Enhanced Bayes classifier consistently performed better than other combinations, such as VGG16, Inception V3, and Inception ResNet-V2, in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. In addition, the proposed method is computationally efficient and requires less training time than deep learning models. The feature extraction process is lightweight and efficient, making the method suitable for real-time medical image classification applications.

records.abstract: Pedestrian trajectory prediction in image-driven perception pipelines is central to intelligent transportation, yet haze degrades image formation, detection, tracking, and forecasting. This study presents the Fog-Aware Physics-Informed Trajectory Predictor (FAPTP), a physics-informed framework for robust pedestrian motion forecasting under haze. It couples a Koschmieder-based physical-prior feature module, an input-dependent selective state-space temporal encoder with cross-layer attention, and a visibility-conditioned heterogeneous graph network for pedestrian and group interactions. Estimated scattering, atmospheric light, and scene-normalized pseudo-depth variables condition temporal encoding, graph interactions, feature fusion, and probabilistic decoding, while temporal representations initialize graph nodes to maintain cross-module flow. A controlled detection-cascaded benchmark is constructed from pedestrian trajectory datasets with four haze-severity levels, shared detector–tracker inputs, and independently specified image and target factors. External predictors are evaluated under a coordinate-only protocol, whereas the complete frame-conditioned model is compared with input-matched controls. Original and behavior-transformed annotations are reported separately, and held-out image-haze/target pairings test cross-transformation generalization. Controlled ablations further isolate the roles of frame evidence, physical-variable correspondence, temporal encoding, and social interaction modeling. Further analyses examine alternative perception pipelines, non-uniform haze, severe missing observations, dense-scene group identification, sequence-length latency, qualitative failure cases, and zero-shot transfer to real daytime light-rain sequences. The results show that atmospheric priors, selective temporal modeling, and visibility-aware social reasoning reduce cascade degradation across the validated operating range.

Accurate Gene Ontology (GO) term prediction is essential for biomedical research, yet broad computational predictors may underperform on lineage-specific proteomes such as Flavobacterium, a genus that includes major aquaculture pathogens. To address this gap, we developed a taxon-specific artificial intelligence framework using all available Universal Protein Resource (UniProt) reference Flavobacterium proteomes (35,554 proteins, 762 GO terms). We used sequence-derived physicochemical descriptors and Evolutionary Scale Modeling 2 (ESM-2) protein language model embeddings as feature vectors for non-graph models and as node attributes for graph models, while a Many-against-Many sequence searching version 2 (MMseqs2) sequence similarity graph was constructed from amino-acid sequence alignments. We evaluated five multi-label classification methods: eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), a deep neural network (DNN), Graph Attention Network (GAT), Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), and Graph Sample and Aggregate (GraphSAGE). At the fixed 0.5 decision threshold, the DNN achieved the highest Micro F1 score (0.9290) and significantly exceeded the other taxon-specific models in aligned paired comparisons. GCN ranked next (0.9033) and significantly exceeded XGBoost (0.8952), whereas GAT (0.8929) was not statistically resolved from XGBoost after multiple-comparison correction. In a controlled evaluation on the same 5333 held-out proteins under symmetric retained-space GO ancestor closure, validation-selected protein-centric F1 was 0.9406 for DNN and 0.9121 for XGBoost, compared with 0.8401 for ProteInfer, 0.6426 for reduced available-component NetGO 4.0, and 0.4741 for DeepGO-SE; both taxon-specific models exceeded all three pretrained general-purpose predictors after paired Holm correction (

These findings establish the value of architecture-specific model selection and aligned evaluation for clade-restricted functional annotation, with potential applications to aquaculture reverse vaccinology and vaccine–target prioritization. records.abstract: Low-altitude farmland remote sensing (FRS) has become an important tool for precision agricultural monitoring. However, existing FRS methods are mainly designed for segmentation with predefined categories, making them insufficient for semantic understanding and unable to support flexible natural-language queries. To address this limitation, we introduce an artificial intelligence-based task, FRS cross-modal retrieval, which aims to retrieve target farmland regions from large-scale remote sensing images using textual descriptions. To support this task, we construct the first Farmland Remote Sensing Cross-Modal Retrieval (FRS-CMR) dataset, containing 67,806 image-text pairs generated through multimodal large language models and expert refinement. Based on FRS-CMR, we propose a Farmland-oriented Multi-Grained Retrieval (FarmMGR) framework for image-text alignment. FarmMGR jointly exploits global scene semantics and local region-level cues to capture both large-scale landscape patterns and fine-grained farmland characteristics. To further improve semantic alignment, we design Prototype-Based Semantic Alignment (PBSA) to alleviate the soft-positive sample problem, Global Semantics Hierarchical Feature Integration (GSHFI) to adaptively fuse global and local representations, and Instance-Level Semantic Relation Modeling (ISRM) to capture relational dependencies among farmland instances. In addition, Memory-Enhanced Cross-Modal Contrastive Learning (MECCL) enlarges the negative sample pool and improves representation discrimination. Extensive experiments on FRS-CMR show that FarmMGR achieves a mean recall of 28.57%, outperforming existing image-text retrieval methods and demonstrating its effectiveness for language-driven farmland remote sensing retrieval.

records.abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) provide neurosurgeons with a powerful tool to accurately identify and remove brain tumors while minimizing damage to healthy tissues. However, conventional HSI systems suffer from insufficient temporal resolution, inadequate spectral resolution for precise tissue differentiation, and high hardware costs that limit clinical accessibility. To address these challenges, we propose a spectral reconstruction method based on a latent diffusion model (LDM), termed the channel encoder latent diffusion model (CE-LDM), which reconstructs high-fidelity HSI from snapshot RGB images captured by standard cameras. This snapshot-based acquisition inherently resolves temporal constraints by freezing tissue motion, while dramatically reducing hardware costs through the use of conventional Red–Green–Blue (RGB) sensors. Given the high-dimensional nature of hyperspectral data, we design a channel encoder to extract prior information, reduce data redundancy, and effectively mitigate the underconstrained problem in spectral reconstruction. Meanwhile, the diffusion model significantly improves spectral fidelity through iterative denoising. Additionally, we design a residual attention denoising network (RADNet) to enhance feature extraction and image detail reconstruction. Tests on in vivo Human Brain HSI dataset validate demonstrates that CE-LDM achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction quality with the lowest computational cost, offering an optimal balance for real-time intraoperative applications, and subsequent classification tasks confirm its clinical applicability and great potential in advancing hyperspectral brain tumor diagnosis.

records.abstract: Accurate reconstruction of the full airflow field is essential for real-time monitoring and control in engineering applications. Although conventional computational fluid dynamics methods offer high accuracy, their computational cost is often prohibitive for real-time scenarios. Data-driven methods present a more efficient alternative; however, their performance is constrained by the sparse observations typically encountered in practical environments. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) alleviate this limitation by incorporating physical laws, yet their practical applicability remains hindered by the difficulty of enforcing complex boundary conditions. To address this challenge, this study proposes a unified hard-constraint approach for airflow field reconstruction that enables numerous, discontinuous, and irregular boundary conditions to be handled simultaneously within a single framework. The proposed method establishes a unified implicit geometry representation for complex boundary conditions by integrating analytical distance functions for regular geometries and neural-network-based distance functions for irregular geometries via R-function-inspired smooth Boolean composition. A customized PINN framework is further developed for airflow field reconstruction by incorporating the proposed implicit boundary representation, sparse observations, and the Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes equations. The proposed framework is validated using both numerical simulations and experimental measurements. In the numerical case without an occupant using 15 sparse observation points, the proposed hard-constraint method reduced the root mean square error and mean absolute error components u by 19.4% and 33.6%, respectively, compared to the soft-constraint method. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach and highlight its potential for practical airflow field reconstruction in complex engineering environments.

records.abstract: Thin plates are common structural elements in engineering. Accurate and efficient prediction of its mechanical properties helps optimize equipment reliability and cost. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are a type of deep learning model that incorporates physical laws, which can solve solid mechanics problems by learning physical principles. However, existing PINNs only consider simple, regular shapes due to the idealized assumptions. PINNs have limited capability to address irregular deformations that often occur during processes such as machining or assembly. Regarding the above issues, this paper first proposed an ideal rectangular plate PINNs (IRP-PINNs) framework under mixed boundary conditions. Accurate deflection predictions for thin-plate boundary loading problems are ensured by explicitly modeling the interaction between loaded and unloaded boundaries in the loss function. Second, based on the Free-Form Deformation (FFD) method, the irregular shape of the thin plate was described in matrix form. Combining matrix and IRP-PINNs, irregularly shaped plate PINNs (ISP-PINNs) and irregularly shaped shell PINNs (ISS-PINNs) were designed. Then, the accuracy of the model predictions was validated through comparison with the finite element method (FEM). Numerical validation shows that the relative error of IRP-PINNs is less than 1%, while the average relative error of ISS-PINNs is less than 2.73%. Finally, the predictive capability and computational efficiency of the model under actual operating conditions were evaluated through experiments. The proposed model can reduce prediction time by nearly tenfold while maintaining computational accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework can efficiently and accurately accomplish the task of predicting thin plate deflection.

records.abstract: This paper proposes an evolvable physics-informed neural network (PINN) for experimental digital twins (EDTs) of industrial systems for real-time modeling and adaptation. The framework integrates three components: system identification with dynamic modeling PINN, stable prediction using temporal contrastive learning, and adaptive parameter learning based on residual adapters. Experiments on permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) demonstrate high data efficiency, improved robustness, and strong generalizability over conventional models, with up to 1.82\times improvement in goodness of fit ({R}^{2}) under extreme data constraints while maintaining mean squared errors (MSEs) at 1{0}^{-1}–1{0}^{-2} under parameter drift. The framework provides a foundation for evaluating system behavior and optimal strategies in dynamic industrial environments.

records.abstract: To address the challenges of real-time observation of gas-solid two-phase flow and the high computational cost/lack of real-time capability of traditional Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations in fluidized bed drying processes, this paper proposes a rapid flow field reconstruction method based on Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). This method integrates sparse observation data with governing flow equations to achieve simultaneous prediction of key physical quantities including gas-phase velocity, solid-phase velocity, pressure, and solid volume fraction. A systematic evaluation was conducted under various conditions: spatial sparsity (20%, 5%, 1%), temporal sparsity (50%, 20%, 10%), noise interference (1%–20%), and cross-temporal extrapolation. Results show that with a spatial sampling rate as low as 5%, PINNs can still accurately reconstruct typical fluidization features such as bubble motion, solid-phase stratification, and pressure gradients. Even under an extreme sparsity of 1%, the overall flow pattern remains correct. Under dual spatio-temporal sparsity, the model demonstrates good information compensation capability, generating continuous and plausible transient evolution. With noise levels up to 20%, reconstruction errors exhibit only minor fluctuations, indicating strong noise resistance. Cross-temporal extrapolation experiments reveal that error growth over unseen time periods is steady and controllable, without non-physical oscillations. This study validates the stability, physical consistency, and robustness of PINNs under complex industrial scenarios involving sparsity, noise, and extrapolation, providing a viable technical pathway for real-time flow field reconstruction and intelligent monitoring in fluidized bed drying processes.

records.abstract: Lattice structures are widely used in advanced engineering because of their lightweight characteristics and tunable mechanical properties. However, precise generative inverse design remains challenging because of the discrete combinatorial design space and nonlinear physical responses. Existing generative approaches often operate open-loop and focus on reproducing statistical distributions, making compliance with prescribed engineering targets difficult. To address this limitation, a performance-feedback-guided generative inverse-design framework integrates reinforcement learning (RL) with a physics-constrained conditional variational autoencoder (PC-VAE). The PC-VAE provides a continuous latent representation of discrete lattice topologies, while a pretrained surrogate supplies immediate performance feedback. The inverse-design stage is formulated as a one-step goal-conditioned contextual decision problem, in which a task-specific proximal policy optimization (PPO) policy learns a distribution over complete latent vectors from surrogate-based rewards. Policy updates increase the likelihood of candidates satisfying prescribed mechanical conditions while retaining alternative topologies. The framework is evaluated in six scenarios involving point-target, interval-constrained, and simultaneous two-property matching. Compared with the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES), PPO achieves comparable target-hit rates and consistently higher candidate uniqueness and topological diversity. Finite-element (FE) analyses of 48 prespecified validation structures were completed successfully. Median absolute surrogate-to-FE discrepancies were 3.03% for energy absorption and 3.88% for peak stress, with 87.50% of discrepancies within 10% for each property. For a given target, the method generates multiple topologically distinct structures with comparable mechanical responses, capturing the one-to-many relationship between prescribed properties and lattice topology. This study provides a flexible framework for target-directed generation of topologically diverse lattice candidates.

records.abstract: Multisource remote sensing image fusion has become an important solution to a long-standing limitation in Earth observation: individual sensors rarely provide high spatial detail, rich spectral information, reliable structural sensitivity, and frequent temporal coverage at the same time. This review examines how deep learning and artificial intelligence are being used to integrate multispectral, hyperspectral, panchromatic, optical, and synthetic aperture radar imagery for more reliable interpretation of complex ground scenes. It provides a technical synthesis of convolutional neural networks, autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, transformer architectures, diffusion models, and hybrid model driven approaches, with attention to their fusion mechanisms, reconstruction behavior, computational demand, and suitability for operational use. Applications include land cover mapping, precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, urban analysis, disaster assessment, and defense related interpretation. Rather than treating each fusion task separately, this review connects sensor heterogeneity, spatial and spectral resolution trade offs, radiometric correction, geometric correction, registration, noise reduction, and fusion level design within a single framework. The analysis indicates that convolutional models remain effective for stable local detail recovery, adversarial learning can improve visual sharpness but may introduce spectral distortion, transformer models better capture long range spatial and spectral relationships, and diffusion models offer refined reconstruction at greater computational cost. The review further identifies open challenges involving misregistration, spectral bias, limited labeled data, weak generalization across sensors, high memory requirements, and limited interpretability. Future progress should prioritize sensor aware learning, self supervised training, uncertainty aware evaluation, lightweight deployment, and application oriented benchmarks to improve reliability in operational Earth observation.

records.abstract: Understanding and replicating human mobility requires not only spatial–temporal accuracy but also an awareness of the cognitive hierarchy underlying real-world travel decisions. Existing approaches often lack interpretability and struggle to represent adaptive behavior under changing constraints. This study proposes a Narrative-to-Action hierarchical large language model agent framework that models human mobility as a cognitively interpretable, multi-level process. The framework decomposes mobility generation into macro-level narrative reasoning, meso-level reflective planning, and micro-level behavioral execution, enabling agents to produce semantically coherent and structurally executable daily schedules while allowing dynamic adjustment in response to contextual changes. A key component is a reflective mechanism drawing on Mobility Entropy by Occupation, which captures heterogeneous behavioral flexibility across occupational groups. Empirical evaluation using travel diary data from Guangzhou demonstrates improved fidelity across spatial, temporal, and semantic dimensions compared to baseline approaches. Overall, by explicitly modeling how individuals reason about and adapt to constraints, the framework provides a behaviorally grounded and interpretable approach for mobility analysis, providing a basis for more transparent future evaluation of policy interventions and equity impacts.

records.abstract: The construction industry requires sustainable alternatives to conventional concrete to reduce environmental impacts while maintaining structural performance. Jute fiber concrete (JFC) is a promising low-carbon material; however, optimizing its mechanical properties is challenging because of complex nonlinear interactions among fiber characteristics and mix-design parameters. This study proposes an integrated framework combining Generative Artificial Intelligence (GEN-AI) with Decision Tree Boosting (DT-Boosting), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and GPR enhanced with Bayesian Optimization (GPR-BO) to predict and optimize JFC mechanical properties. An experimental dataset containing six input variables were expanded using a Large Language Model-based GEN-AI approach and validated through distribution analysis, boxplot comparisons, and Kendall correlation analysis. GPR-based models significantly outperformed DT-Boosting, reducing prediction errors by approximately 40–50%. The GPR-BO achieved the most consistent performance, with testing R^{2} values of 0.9242 for compressive strength and 0.9682 for tensile strength. However, the SHAP and Partial Dependence Plot analyses identified jute fiber volume fraction and fiber content as the most influential parameters, while the water–cement ratio exhibited a strong negative effect. Probabilistic validation confirmed accurate reproduction of strength distributions. Furthermore, integrating GPR-BO with NSGA-II enabled inverse mix design, automatically generating optimized JFC mixtures satisfying user-defined mechanical performance requirements. The optimization employed six mix-design decision variables and minimized both normalized prediction error and fiber volume fraction to identify Pareto-optimal solutions. The resulting framework extends forward prediction to practical inverse design, reducing trial-and-error experimentation and material waste while supporting resource-efficient, performance-based, and sustainable concrete mix development for engineering applications.

records.abstract: Agriculture is still a crucial global pillar of the world economy, ensuring food security and livelihood. But changing climate conditions and increasing reliance on the Internet of Things (IoT) based precision agriculture have brought new challenges, mainly cybersecurity. Cooperative Smart Farming (CSF) schemes promote resource pooling among small farmers and thus, the adoption of cutting-edge technologies. Although democratizing precision farming also makes it more accessible to cyber threats. To sort out all these problems, the proposed method introduces a secure federated learning framework along with blockchain-based authentication for anomaly detection in CSFs. The proposed method employs a federated transfer learning-based shadow attention mechanism, in conjunction with the Zeiler and Fergus network, to amplify the performance of the anomaly detection technique. This allows farms to detect threats in premises while protecting data privacy, as only model updates that are encrypted are transmitted. A blockchain-backed decentralized authentication scheme based on the proof of authentication consensus protocol is built to provide trust and resistance to tampering. Moreover, the random k-sparsification technique with changing rank adjustment has a positive impact on communication efficiency, which results in the same level of accuracy but with less communication overhead. The proposed method is executed on four datasets, CSE-CIS-IDS2018, MQTTset, ToN-IoT, and Edge IoT, achieving classification accuracies of 99.99%,99.93%,99.94%, and 99.91%, respectively, and it performs better than the current techniques. This comprehensive framework provides a scalable and trusted method for anomaly detection in CSFs, enabling resilient, privacy-preserving, and intelligent smart farming ecosystems.

records.abstract: Human-robot collaborative assembly (HRCA) extends traditional manual assembly by synergizing human cognitive flexibility with robotic precision, and has become an important manufacturing paradigm in Industry 5.0. However, this synergy is frequently compromised by subtle human errors, whose automated detection presents a formidable challenge. This difficulty is fundamentally rooted in the visual ambiguity arising from high similarity in color, texture, and geometry between components and their assembly substrates. These conditions create low-contrast scenarios that obscure the fine-grained anomaly detection, such as minor positional offsets, rotational skews, and incorrect part substitutions. To address this challenge, this paper introduces a novel artificial intelligence (AI)-driven vision framework for fine-grained anomaly detection, enabling reliable in-process quality control for HRCA. The framework integrates three synergistic modules in a cohesive pipeline involving state perception, recognition and localization, and state discrimination. Firstly, a multi-task Keypoint Transformer U-Net (KP-TransUNet) performs concurrent component segmentation and keypoint detection with sub-pixel accuracy, establishing a robust foundation for geometric registration even in visually challenging environments. Subsequently, an improved You Only Look Once version 11 (Improved-YOLO11) algorithm precisely identifies and localizes assembly components. Finally, an Intersection over Union (IoU)-mask matching strategy combines box-level semantic matching with mask-level geometric deviation analysis to quantitatively discriminate among six typical assembly states. The efficacy of the proposed framework was empirically validated through a comprehensive case study on a satellite box assembly, achieving an overall anomaly detection accuracy of 97.30%.

records.abstract: The seismic fragility of masonry buildings have been ubiquitously discussed in multiple zones worldwide. However, field inspection and data collection after earthquakes demonstrate the disadvantages of being time-consuming and labour-intensive, which poses a challenge for quickly obtaining the seismic fragility features of masonry structure clusters. To improve the efficiency of earthquake damage prediction and the rapid estimation of the seismic fragility of masonry structures, a seismic fragility prediction model for masonry buildings involving gradient boosting machine (GBM), categorical boosting (CatBoost), and feedforward neural network (FNN) methods was developed via intelligent ensemble algorithms and deep learning techniques. Using dynamic response analysis and earthquake risk assessment processes, dynamic responsiveness, hazard analysis, and intelligent model development were conducted on 2,598,972 accelerations monitored by the Wenchuan earthquake (May 12, 2008) array group in China. A dataset of 2211 masonry buildings (investigated by the author) in Dujiangyan city was thoroughly analysed, and a fragility matrix considering the optimised seismic vulnerability (damage) grade was proposed. The input variables of the learning model were the construction year, major story, foundation, function, and instrument intensity; moreover, a sensitivity analysis of the characteristic parameters was conducted. The optimised vulnerability (damage) grade of masonry structures was used as the output variable of the integrated and deep learning models. Using the established database, 20% and 80% of the structural damage instances were stratified and selected for testing and training model development, respectively. An analytical (precision-recall) curve was generated to evaluate the correlation between the predicted parameters of a learning model. To confirm the predictive precision of the developed learning model, a set of seismic fragility comparison curves for masonry buildings considering intelligent and empirical data-driven strategies was generated.

records.abstract: Autonomous driving has the potential to greatly enhance road safety, traffic efficiency, and overall transportation effectiveness. The decision-making module serves as the core intelligence of the system, producing high-level commands for lane keeping, lane changing, and adaptive cruise control. Deep reinforcement learning has emerged as a pivotal approach in this domain, owing to its capacity to learn driving strategies through environmental interaction. This paper presents a systematic review of decision-making methods based on deep reinforcement learning for autonomous vehicles. It starts by outlining the general architecture of autonomous driving systems and emphasizing the central role of the decision-making module. The paper then explains the theoretical foundations of deep reinforcement learning, along with their applicability in driving decision tasks. Through a range of common driving scenarios, including lane keeping, lane changing, overtaking, and intersection navigation, the paper analyzes the decision-making advantages of deep reinforcement learning in complex and dynamic settings. Furthermore, it addresses key challenges in applying deep reinforcement learning to driving tasks. Compared to existing reviews, this study provides a systematic analysis of deep reinforcement learning in multiple decision-making scenarios for autonomous driving, overcoming the limitation of previous reviews that often focus on single scenarios. Adopting a progressive narrative structure, from single lateral or longitudinal control to increasingly complex tasks involving lateral-longitudinal coordination, it systematically clarifies the characteristics of different deep reinforcement learning algorithms and their applicable conditions. This structured approach helps researchers select appropriate algorithms and fusion strategies when facing driving scenarios of varying complexity.

records.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a mesh-free paradigm for solving Partial Differential Equations (PDEs), yet a spectral bias severely limits their ability to resolve high-frequency components of oscillatory problems, and conventional Fourier-feature remedies scale exponentially with dimension. To overcome these limitations, we propose Separated-Variable Spectral Neural Networks (SV-SNN), a physics-informed framework with three core innovations. First, a separated-variable spectral representation expresses multivariate solutions as sums of $N$ separable modes, each a product of univariate adaptive Fourier spectral factors with $K$ frequencies per direction; this unites the dimensional scalability of variable separation with the frequency control of spectral methods, reducing the number of trainable parameters from order ${K}^{d}$ of tensor-product spectral bases to order $dNK$, linear in the dimension $d$, while admitting closed-form spatial derivatives through a hybrid differentiation strategy. Second, a characteristic-frequency multi-level sampling strategy allocates spectral resources across low-, characteristic-, and high-frequency bands, thereby targeting spectral bias and reducing sensitivity to frequency-estimation errors, with the characteristic frequency estimated automatically when not available a priori. Third, an effective-rank diagnostic derived from the singular value decomposition of the residual Jacobian quantifies spectral-bias severity a posteriori, explaining why standard architectures fail on oscillatory problems and guiding architecture selection. Across nine benchmarks—high-wavenumber heat and Helmholtz equations, nonlinear elliptic and Poisson problems on complex domains, and incompressible Navier–Stokes flows—SV-SNN achieves lower error than every competing baseline in matched-budget comparisons, by factors of 1.9 to 94, and remains more accurate even when baselines are afforded 15 to 200 times more parameters. Training completes within 11 to 34 s per problem on a single graphics processing unit. SV-SNN thus provides an accurate and parameter-efficient framework for wave propagation, heat conduction, and incompressible flow simulation. The source code is available at https://github.com/xgxgnpu/Physics-informed-vibe-coding/tree/main/SV-SNN.

records.abstract: Online battery management requires accurate state-of-charge (SOC) and state-of-health (SOH) estimates within strict memory and timing budgets. To address these constraints, this work investigates how stateful long short-term memory (LSTM) networks with multi-layer perceptron (MLP) heads can be optimized for embedded artificial intelligence (AI), using structured pruning and recurrent-weight quantization to reduce memory and computational costs while retaining estimation accuracy on an STM32H753ZI microcontroller. Using the open Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) Cycle Ageing Dataset, full-precision models provide the accuracy reference against which the compressed variants are evaluated. Long-horizon replay yields mean absolute error (MAE) values of 2.3–2.8 percentage points for SOC and 0.9–1.5 for SOH, showing that compression largely preserves accuracy. The evaluated 30% pruning configuration reduces flash by 37.2% and 43.3% in the available firmware builds and inference time by 42.9% and 44.0% in the recorded hardware-in-the-loop benchmarks for SOC and SOH, respectively. The analytical complexity model relates computational savings to pruning fraction and network dimensions. Quantization reduces flash by 49.7% and 55.9% relative to the respective full-precision models, but raises runtime in the mixed-precision implementation. Together, the study provides a reproducible reference for resource-efficient embedded battery-state estimation.

records.abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting is essential for wind farm operation and grid integration. However, newly built wind farms often have limited historical data, restricting the performance of data-driven models. Under data scarcity, conventional deep learning models tend to overfit, while direct transfer learning may introduce irrelevant source-domain information when source and target farms differ. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a component-aware progressive transfer learning method for newly built wind farms. Relevant source wind farms are first selected based on combined power-sequence and meteorological similarity to reduce negative transfer. The original power sequence is then decomposed into trend and fluctuation components, which are modeled using a multilayer perceptron and a conditional generative adversarial network, respectively, and integrated through attention-based fusion. Rather than fine-tuning the entire model simultaneously, the proposed strategy progressively adapts the trend predictor, fluctuation model, and fusion module. Experiments on three newly built wind farm datasets yielded root mean square errors of 0.8850, 2.5060, and 5.0429 MW, representing reductions of 35.29%, 25.71%, and 33.03% over the best-performing benchmarks. On a United States dataset, the method achieved a root mean square error of 0.6543 MW and a coefficient of determination of 0.9870 for 15-min-ahead forecasting, while retaining its advantage over the comparison methods for forecasts 30 and 60 min ahead. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of source relevance selection, component-specific modeling, and progressive transfer learning under limited target-domain data.

records.abstract: Accurate safety-state measurement of the three-electric system in new energy vehicles is essential for ensuring reliable and secure operation. This paper proposes an artificial-intelligence-assisted safety measurement framework that integrates a searchable encryption mechanism with Enhanced Physics-Informed Neural Networks (EPINNs). In the proposed framework, the searchable encryption module supports privacy-preserving storage and retrieval of multi-source measurement data, while EPINNs serve as the core Artificial Intelligence (AI) model for multi-parameter state estimation and fault identification. A lightweight searchable encryption scheme based on block mapping is first designed to achieve feature-level obfuscation and protect sensitive measurement data. Then, an EPINNs-based state estimation model is developed by incorporating data-driven learning, subsystem physical constraints, and energy-consistency terms to enhance robustness under noisy sensor data. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves improved performance compared with conventional Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models in battery state-of-health estimation, motor fault detection under injected fault conditions, and microgrid load measurement, with the motor fault detection accuracy exceeding 95% under the tested conditions. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective and secure technical solution for intelligent safety monitoring of new energy vehicle three-electric systems.
