records.abstract: Classical Forrestal penetration calculations are attractive because they are explicit, but their empirical strength-only resistance term is too restrictive for heterogeneous concrete-penetration data. This study derives a closed-form resistance equation from a governed literature dataset, reducing 497 raw records from 41 source blocks to 443 useable records from 37 sources through duplicate removal, governed density completion, deep-penetration filtering, and descriptor-only anomaly screening. Forrestal inversion maps each measured penetration depth to an operator-consistent effective resistance target described by mechanics-informed dimensionless descriptors. The artificial-intelligence contribution is a constrained equation-discovery workflow in which a categorical gradient-boosting model learns the nonlinear resistance surface, Shapley additive explanations restrict the analytical term family, and limited-memory Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno optimization with bound constraints identifies equation coefficients under a forward penetration-depth objective. The engineering contribution is a 16-term explicit resistance law that replaces the empirical resistance relation inside the Forrestal operator while retaining its deterministic calculation form. On the 89-record held-out set, the equation gives a coefficient of determination of 0.9543 and a mean absolute percentage error of 14.88%, compared with 0.9206 and 24.44% for classical Forrestal and 0.9551 and 13.95% for the nonlinear resistance-reference model; its mean prediction-to-measurement ratio is 0.984. Repeated random, source-grouped, strength-stratified, out-of-distribution, input-uncertainty, and density-robustness tests bound the useable domain. The 80–120 MPa interval remains cautionary because of weaker held-out accuracy and limited cross-source support.

records.abstract:
Reusable launch vehicles undergo severe thermal cycling, and cryogenic storage conditions introduce strong, nonlinear distortions in guided ultrasonic wave signals used for structural health monitoring. These temperature-induced effects obscure damage sensitive features and limit the robustness of both conventional compensation techniques and purely data driven learning models.

This paper proposes a physics informed machine learning framework, termed the Guided Wave Physics-Informed Generative Adversarial Network, to compensate cryogenic guided ultrasonic wave distortions in a physically consistent manner. The artificial intelligence component is realized through generative adversarial learning and is applied to cryogenic guided-wave temperature compensation The model adopts a residual generative formulation in the Hilbert-envelope domain and integrates adversarial sequence learning with wave-physics priors through curvature based regularization and peak morphology constraints. These physics-informed components explicitly suppress nonphysical temporal artifacts and preserve the modal structure of guided-wave responses, enabling stable compensation across varying cryogenic conditions.

Experiments conducted on an aluminum alloy plate under liquid-nitrogen cooling–heating cycles demonstrate that GW-PIGAN achieves high-fidelity reconstruction while maintaining consistent performance across varying reference temperatures. Compared with purely data-driven baselines, the proposed physics-informed formulation exhibits improved stability, physical plausibility, and generalization under extreme thermal conditions.

By embedding guided-wave physics into generative learning, the proposed framework provides a practical and interpretable physics-informed machine learning approach for cryogenic structural health monitoring. It also establishes a methodological basis for future monitoring applications in reusable aerospace structures under extreme cryogenic conditions.

records.abstract: Additively manufactured aluminium alloys joined by friction stir welding exhibit great potential for large-scale structural applications, yet their fatigue life prediction remains challenging due to the complex influence of internal defects and process-induced microstructural heterogeneity. To address this issue, a defect-based, physics-informed neural network framework was proposed for fatigue life prediction of additively manufactured AlSi7Mg friction stir welded joints. A multi-route physics-informed modeling strategy is introduced, incorporating physical prior knowledge through feature engineering, loss function design, and adaptive feature weighting. Four data augmentation methods are employed to enhance data diversity and model robustness, and the results show that among these approaches, Precise Physics Law (PPL) yields the best overall performance. The proposed Defect and Multi-Physics Coupled Informed Neural Network (DM-PINN) dynamically adjusts the weights of physical loss terms based on defect and multi-physics features, achieving a better balance between data-driven learning and physical consistency. Experimental results demonstrate that the DM-PINN model outperforms both conventional artificial neural networks and standard physics-informed neural networks in terms of prediction accuracy, generalization capability, and physical interpretability. The model successfully predicts conditional fatigue limits under different processing conditions with errors below 15%, providing a reliable tool for fatigue life assessment and process optimization of defect-sensitive additive manufacturing components.

records.abstract: Proportional delay differential equations model systems that depend on proportionally scaled historical states and arise in applications including astrophysics, engineering, and biology. However, proportional delays may span a wide, time-varying range and depend on states arbitrarily close to the initial time. Consequently, conventional discretization-based methods, particularly finite-difference-type approaches, require careful treatment of delayed arguments and can be computationally challenging. This study develops a unified physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for forward simulation and inverse parameter identification in proportional delay ordinary and partial differential equations. The framework incorporates differential equation residuals, initial or boundary conditions, and observational data into a composite loss function. An adaptive weighting strategy balances competing loss terms, while two-stage optimization and a multi-stage residual correction procedure improve training stability and accuracy. Numerical experiments show stable, high-precision solutions for highly oscillatory equations, the handling of challenging high-order nonlinear cases, and accurate identification of unknown delay parameters and coefficients under noisy or sparse data. Under stated assumptions, the Appendix further shows that a sufficiently small physics-informed loss yields a small solution approximation error. The proposed framework thus provides a mesh-free, effective, and theoretically supported approach for proportional-delay systems when conventional discretization-based methods are difficult to apply.

records.abstract: Guided wave (GW)-based damage localization in carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites is fundamentally challenged by thermal variations and sparse sensor configurations, which induce severe baseline distortions and imaging artifacts. Traditional physical algorithms suffer from geometric ambiguity, while purely data-driven artificial intelligence (AI) models are hindered by opaque interpretability and prohibitive data dependency. This paper proposes a physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) framework, an artificial-intelligence-driven approach, for few-shot damage localization under thermal variations. The network is architected with a dual-stream input design, comprising a data-driven layer enhanced by a one-dimensional coordinate attention (1D-CA) mechanism and a physics-informed layer built upon a differentiable time-of-flight (TOF) physical imaging layer. A hybrid physics-constrained loss function is formulated to suppress non-physical artifacts and enforce physical consistency. GW signals are experimentally collected from manufactured CFRP composite plates, and a comparative investigation is performed to thoroughly assess the PIDL performance. Results indicate that:(1) The presence of physical penalties effectively mitigates artifacts and achieves robust localization across thermal gradients; (2) The model demonstrates superior spatial generalization that the integration of acoustic physical constraints acts as a crucial regularization mechanism, maintaining a highly accurate mean relative error (MRE) of 3.88% on completely unseen damage coordinates; (3) By implementing a few-shot transfer learning strategy, the PIDL model shows adaptability for dynamic operational environments (45 degrees Celsius (°C)-75 degrees Celsius (°C)). This work offers a physically interpretable and data-efficient paradigm for structural health monitoring (SHM) in dynamic operational environments.

records.abstract: The accelerated deployment of smart grids has intensified the need for real-time insulator monitoring and health diagnostics, particularly for the early detection of thermal faults. While infrared thermography enables non-contact fault localization, industrial thermal imagers are often constrained by insufficient spatial resolution and inherent sensor artifacts, compromising both image quality and thermal interpretability. To address information compression and undersampling while recovering relative thermal-pattern information and structural representations, we introduce the Fidelity-aware InfraRed Enhancement Network (FIRE-Net), a physics-informed transformer for artificial intelligence (AI)-driven super-resolution of pseudo-color infrared images. The model incorporates an infrared denoising block to suppress sensor noise, employs learnable unsharp masking and high-frequency attention modules to recover structural details, and is supervised by a thermal-consistency loss function that constrains relative thermal patterns in a normalized palette-derived temperature-proxy domain. On the insulator infrared test set, FIRE-Net achieves peak signal-to-noise ratio values of 31.0021 dB (dB) (×2) and 27.6765 dB (×4), with structural similarity index scores of 0.9143 and 0.8591, respectively. The model also improves downstream detection performance, attaining mean average precision at intersection over union = 0.50 values of 0.857 (×2) and 0.904 (×4), representing improvements of 0.102 and 0.111 over the low-resolution baseline. Its cross-scenario performance is further evaluated on a hold-out photovoltaic dataset. We further analyze computational efficiency and outline future research directions, including domain-extended training and lightweight deployment. The results demonstrate that incorporating physics-inspired priors into super-resolution models effectively improves normalized temperature-proxy consistency and practical detection performance. The source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/Sevil-cy/FIRE-Net.

records.abstract: The reliable prediction of the full constitutive response in recycled aggregate concrete is frequently compromised by the high stochasticity of material properties and the unavailability of peak parameters during the structural design phase. This study develops a two-stage sequential learning framework for the end-to-end reconstruction of stress–strain trajectories without requiring predefined peak inputs. The architecture integrates gradient boosting surrogate models for peak stress and strain estimation with a physics-informed long short-term memory network for full-curve generation. By embedding failure constraints based on energy conservation alongside monotonicity and boundary priors into the learning process, the framework effectively suppresses non-physical behavior in the softening regime. Comparative evaluations demonstrate that the proposed system exhibits superior robustness and morphological fidelity, achieving a curve-level coefficient of determination of 0.923 and a mean dynamic time warping distance of 27.91. The framework remains stable under ten percent data contamination and utilizes quantile regression to provide quantified prediction intervals that address predictive uncertainty. Furthermore, analysis of the generated curves identifies the enhanced deformation capacity of high-replacement recycled aggregates can compensate for strength loss in high-porosity matrices. The energy toughness ratio is primarily governed by the aggregate replacement ratio rather than matrix strength, providing a standardized measure for the brittle-to-ductile transition. This research offers a computationally efficient numerical tool for characterizing sustainable concrete, ensuring that predicted responses are both mathematically optimized and thermodynamically consistent with fundamental failure mechanisms.

records.abstract: Autonomous driving systems are increasingly required to operate safely in dynamic and cognitively complex environments, yet the cognitive and mental states of vehicle occupants remain underexplored relative to vehicle perception and planning. This paper presents a multi-task electroencephalography (EEG, the recording of brain electrical activity)-based deep learning framework addressing four cognitive-state tasks relevant to autonomous driving: hazard perception, trust prediction, cognitive load estimation via EEG and heart-rate-variability (HRV) fusion, and brain-computer interface (BCI) motor-imagery classification. The framework is first developed on physiologically parameterized synthetic EEG signals derived from the structural characteristics of five open-source datasets (DEAP, DREAMER, PhysioNet, SEED, OpenNeuro); five classifiers — random forest, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), support vector machine, a convolutional-recurrent neural network (CNN-RNN), and an EEG Transformer — attain near-ceiling accuracy on this synthetic benchmark, reflecting the separability built into the simulation rather than real-world decodability. To test this directly, the framework is subsequently validated on genuine human recordings from PhysioNet (21 subjects, motor imagery) and DREAMER (23 subjects, valence/arousal ratings used as proxies for trust-related affect and cognitive load, with electrocardiogram-derived HRV for multimodal fusion). On real data, accuracy falls to 51%–77% within-subject and to 44%–59% — at or below chance for some tasks — under subject-independent evaluation; permutation testing and a spectral comparison against the synthetic signals help explain this gap. Real HRV fusion yields a modest but genuine gain for cognitive-load estimation (+4.8 percentage points over EEG alone), unlike the synthetic-data result. No open dataset with a hazard-perception paradigm was available for real-data validation, which is reported here as an explicit limitation. Together, these synthetic and real-data results provide an artificial-intelligence-based benchmark for neurophysiological human-state monitoring in autonomous driving that is transparent about what is demonstrated versus what remains to be validated before real-time, in-vehicle deployment.

records.abstract: Reinforced concrete (RC) beams often sustain flexural damage during their service life due to overloading or environmental degradation, requiring effective repair solutions; however, strengthening with carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) layers is limited by premature debonding of the CFRP from the concrete surface. In this paper, CFRP fan spikes were employed for anchoring the CFRP layers at the RC damaged beam ends. Engineered cementitious composites (ECC) were employed to form a crack control layer beneath the beam and in the damaged areas. Six RC beams were studied experimentally, analytically and by machine learning methods including control specimens, damaged specimens subjected to 25% and 50% of the maximum bending capacity, and damaged specimens strengthened with the CFRP fan spike system. Experimental results showed that the fan spike anchors efficiently prevent CFRP separation while also repairing and enhancing the mechanical properties of damaged RC beams. The proposed reinforcement technique greatly enhances stiffness and reduces crack width, making it a reliable option for repairing damaged RC beams. Analytical models supported the experimental findings and also an optimized machine learning (ML) model, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), can predict the unseen experimental response with 0.6-6.7% errors.

records.abstract: Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in clinical diagnosis and treatment. However, existing deep-learning methods can suffer from semantic gaps in encoder-decoder architectures, while the quadratic cost of self-attention limits computational scalability as the input sequence length increases. To address these issues, we propose a Convolutional Neural Network and Transformer-based model, Segmented Sparse Transformer Network, abbreviated as SegSparseTransNet. The innovation lies in: (1) We propose the Segmented Sparse Attention (SSA) mechanism to reduce computational complexity and ensure the global perception ability of the model. (2) We design the Dynamic Skip Attention (DSA) block to optimize feature fusion between the encoder and decoder. (3) We present the Cross-Modal Fusion (CMF) block to enhance the expressive power of advanced semantic features. Experiments on several medical image datasets show that the proposed SegSparseTransNet outperforms existing methods in multiple key metrics, such as mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) and mean Dice Coefficient (mDice), demonstrating its effectiveness and competitiveness in medical image segmentation tasks. The code is available at: https://github.com/wuxianghu/SegSparseTransNet.git.

records.abstract: The mechanical response of history-dependent materials depends on loading paths and thermomechanical histories, rendering neural network-based constitutive modeling challenging. Existing methods typically establish global memory based on historical sequences, requiring large model scales and extensive training data. Targeting materials whose states can be fully described by finite-dimensional internal variables, this paper proposes a Local Decoupling Evolution Operator Network (LDEONet) grounded in the Markovian property. The proposed framework explicitly decomposes the internal variable evolution model into evolution direction and evolution intensity. Using the thermomechanical cycle of shape memory polymers as a case study, eight models are trained, and a series of experiments are designed, including path generalization tests, discretization generalization tests, and decoupling ablation studies. Experimental results demonstrate that the model contains 242 trainable parameters and requires only about 1/175 of the training curves compared to sequence-based models, while making predictions without needing historical memory. The model maintains accurate predictions across various unseen loading paths and unseen step sizes, and the decoupling architecture is shown to provide structural guarantees for generalization. The Local Decoupling Evolution Operator Network thus offers a lightweight modeling approach with both path generalization and discretization generalization capabilities for history-dependent materials that possess explicit internal variable models.

records.abstract: Accurate chiller energy consumption prediction is critical for enhancing heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) system efficiency and building energy conservation. However, existing models exhibit limited generalization under variable operating conditions and sparse data, and conventional physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) struggle with adaptive physical weight adjustment and deep network convergence. To address these issues, this study proposes a condition-aware adaptive physics-informed residual network (CAA-PIResNet) for chiller energy consumption modeling. A one-dimensional residual network (ResNet) is adopted as the backbone to extract nonlinear features and alleviate the vanishing gradient problem. The Stoecker semi-empirical model provides a chiller-specific physical prior, while a fuzzy neural network (FNN)-based condition-aware mechanism adjusts the data loss and Stoecker-based physics-guided loss weights according to operating conditions. Experiments are conducted to evaluate prediction accuracy, physical interpretability, computational cost, noise robustness, data efficiency, and generalization performance. Results demonstrate that CAA-PIResNet outperforms benchmark models. When trained using only 10% of the available training data, CAA-PIResNet remains stable and achieves at least 12.05% lower mean absolute error (MAE) than the benchmark models. In part-load-ratio (PLR) hold-out experiments, it reduces MAE and root mean square error (RMSE) by 8.21% and 10.05%, respectively, compared with the Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN). The learned adaptive weights and semi-empirical coefficients demonstrate operating-condition-dependent loss balancing and stable physical parameter calibration, supporting the effectiveness of the proposed semi-empirical prior and adaptive mechanism.

records.abstract: Concrete mix design is a nonlinear, constraint-sensitive problem in which empirical approaches require repeated adjustments and rarely account explicitly for predictive uncertainty. This study develops an artificial intelligence-based, uncertainty-aware surrogate-assisted optimization framework for concrete mixtures under engineering constraints. A database of 1508 experimental observations from heterogeneous sources was harmonized through physical plausibility screening and evaluated using leakage-resistant, composition-family-grouped validation. An artificial neural network surrogate was optimized through hyperparameter search and enhanced with physics-informed features and synthetic data generated by a conditional Wasserstein generative adversarial network, followed by local real-data support filtering, with physical plausibility and cross-model consistency assessed as complementary credibility diagnostics. Predictive disagreement across an ensemble was empirically calibrated and incorporated into the strength constraint through a conservative lower bound. On an independent test set, the final hybrid surrogate achieved a mean absolute error of 2.32 MPa, a root mean squared error of 3.16 MPa, a coefficient of determination of 0.951, and a mean absolute percentage error of 9.28%. Constrained cost minimization employed particle swarm optimization, a genetic algorithm, and simulated annealing. Computational candidate mixtures were identified for ordinary 25-MPa concrete, supplementary cementitious material-based 25-MPa concrete, and high-strength 65-MPa concrete. For supplementary cementitious material-based candidates, predicted cement content decreased by approximately 19–21% while satisfying surrogate-based constraints. The high-strength candidates exhibited greater uncertainty and cross-model disagreement; two of three failed the cross-model target check. These findings support computational mixture screening, not experimentally verified performance; targeted laboratory testing remains necessary before implementation.
